# Project template

> Owner: Team lead · Agent: read-only

Template version: **1.7-ft**: 1.7 plus the feature experiment (SQA-interns/feature-testing): a fixed API contract (`02_design/api-contract.md`, AR-09), run type, feature and base run in `run-config.md` and `run-log.json` (`experiment`), and the hidden oracle's pass rates in the report (`results/oracle/`). Before that, **1.7** (1.6 without any usage panel or /cost step: every number is calculated from the session transcript and git, hooks build the report when the session ends, and nothing is typed or copied by hand; the report shows approval prompts and no longer compares against a harness total. The phase documents are committed once per phase, a targeted survivor round can decide the gate without a confirming full run, the verify skill has a traceability helper (`trace-ac.mjs`) and warns against the offline dependency scan, the agent no longer audits commit subjects, and the report fills the Run, Time, Commits and Cost sections of `run-summary.md`. 1.6 was 1.5 plus stricter commit rules (whole subject line at most 72 characters, one category per commit, layered build and test commits, commit before the next change), a post-run report with separate tables, run toggles and the environment of each run. 1.5 was 1.4 plus a fixed quality gate (mutation >= 90 %, line >= 95 %) instead of record-only thresholds, a staged phase 5 with at most three survivor rounds, and acceptance criteria, end-to-end scenarios and answers to the open questions as inputs, so that runs are comparable and cost to reach the gate is what differs. 1.4 was 1.3 plus: coverage and mutation measured in phase 5 and run once on final code, pre-approved findings, acceptance-test self-check, nginx Host and rate-limit requirements; vitest 4.1.11 pin; report fixes: short run name in charts, distinct commit colour, cost check from panel numbers entered in usage.md. 1.3 was 1.2 plus richer statistics: clock tool and unique run id, waits and agent time, deviations, environment, commits with cost, measurement scope, transcript backup, post-run report). Increase it whenever a file in section 2 changes; each run records it in `run-config.md`.

Humans start here; agents start at `AGENTS.md`. To execute a run, follow `Run_Guide.md`.

## Folders

| Folder | Content | Phase |
|---|---|---|
| `01_input/00_general/` | Rules, phases, skills, quality and security baselines for every project | all |
| `01_input/01_project/00_setup/` | Run configuration, secrets list, tech stack, environments | 0 |
| `01_input/01_project/01_requirements/` | Stories, business rules, scope, answered questions, acceptance criteria, end-to-end scenarios | 1 |
| `01_input/01_project/02_design/` | Architecture, security requirements, quality requirements | 2 |
| `02_output/` | Everything the agent produces (docs, code, logs) | 0-7 |
| `03_statistics/` | Experiment measurement (not part of the project) | all |

Project folder numbers match the phase that first uses them; later phases (3-7) use inputs from these folders and the general rules.

## 1. Fill in (human, for each project or run)

| File | What goes in it |
|---|---|
| `01_input/01_project/00_setup/run-config.md` | model, effort, run label, operator, machine, plan, permission mode, run type, feature, base run (every run); the run id is generated |
| `01_input/01_project/00_setup/secrets.env.example` | every secret the project needs (names only); copy to `.env` and fill the values there |
| `01_input/01_project/00_setup/tech-stack.md` | every platform, dependency and tool with exact versions |
| `01_input/01_project/00_setup/environments.md` | environments, settings, external services |
| `01_input/01_project/00_setup/pre-approved.md` | findings the human already decided (the agent records them without asking) |
| `01_input/01_project/01_requirements/user-stories.md` | user stories |
| `01_input/01_project/01_requirements/business-rules.md` | business rules, data fields, glossary |
| `01_input/01_project/01_requirements/scope.md` | in/out of scope, priorities, open questions with their answers |
| `01_input/01_project/01_requirements/acceptance-criteria.md` | the acceptance criteria, an input: the agent does not derive them |
| `01_input/01_project/01_requirements/e2e-scenarios.md` | the end-to-end scenarios, one test each, an input |
| `01_input/01_project/02_design/architecture.md` | components, constraints, interfaces |
| `01_input/01_project/02_design/security-requirements.md` | security level, authentication, personal data, project requirements |
| `01_input/01_project/02_design/quality-requirements.md` | non-functional requirements, thresholds, mutation scope, extra done criteria |
| `01_input/01_project/02_design/api-contract.md` | the fixed REST API (paths, fields, status codes, local test settings) that external checks rely on |
| `03_statistics/usage.md` | prices before the run (one row per model id, shape as in the file); nothing else |

Order: fill `01_requirements/` and `02_design/`, then `00_setup/`, then start the agent. It checks everything else in phase 0 and asks for whatever is missing.

## 2. Do not touch (change only when revising the template itself)

- `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, `Run_Guide.md`
- everything in `01_input/00_general/`:
  - `working-rules.md`, `phases.md`, `engineering-standards.md`
  - `quality/definition-of-done.md`, `quality/severity-scale.md`, `quality/test-strategy.md`, `quality/measurement-scope.md`
  - `security/security-baseline.md`
  - `skills/preflight/SKILL.md`, `skills/write-acceptance-tests/SKILL.md`, `skills/verify-release/SKILL.md`
- `03_statistics/metrics.md`, `03_statistics/run-log.template.json`, `03_statistics/tools/` (the post-run measuring, report and transcript-export scripts)

## 3. Written by the agent (read, do not edit)

- `02_output/README.md` and one README per component
- `02_output/docs/`: `00_preflight-report.md`, `00_input-manifest.sha256` (frozen once written), `00_progress.md`, `01_requirements-check.md`, `02_specification.md`, `02_contracts/`, `03_acceptance-manifest.sha256`, `03_test-strategy.md`, `06_verification-report.md`, `decisions-log.md`, `release-notes.md`
- `02_output/logs/`, all source code and tests in `02_output/`
- repository files required by ES-03 at the repository root: `.gitattributes`, `.gitignore`
- `03_statistics/run-log.json` (through `tools/stat.mjs` and by hand), `03_statistics/run-summary.md`
- written by the post-run session: `03_statistics/results/` (report, measurements, usage summary, commits, readable transcript) and `03_statistics/data/` (transcript backup, committed with the run)

Any change to sections 1 and 2 during a run is detected in phase 6 by comparing `00_input-manifest.sha256`.

## Rules for editing this template

- Start every Markdown file with `> Owner: … · Read in: … · Agent: …` (after the front matter in a `SKILL.md`; agent-written skeletons use `> Written in: … · Source: … · Agent: writes`) and add it to the right list above.
- State each rule once; link to it elsewhere. Write constraints ("Do not …"); procedures go in skills.
- One topic per file, no fixed length: split a file when it covers two topics or a reader needs only half of it. Versions appear only in `tech-stack.md`.

## Folders

| Folder | Content | Phase |
|---|---|---|
| `01_input/00_general/` | Rules, phases, skills, quality and security baselines for every project | all |
| `01_input/01_project/00_setup/` | Run configuration, secrets list, tech stack, environments | 0 |
| `01_input/01_project/01_requirements/` | Stories, business rules, scope, answered questions, acceptance criteria, end-to-end scenarios | 1 |
| `01_input/01_project/02_design/` | Architecture, security requirements, quality requirements | 2 |
| `02_output/` | Everything the agent produces (docs, code, logs) | 0-7 |
| `03_statistics/` | Experiment measurement (not part of the project) | all |

Project folder numbers match the phase that first uses them; later phases (3-7) use inputs from these folders and the general rules.

## 1. Fill in (human, for each project or run)

| File | What goes in it |
|---|---|
| `01_input/01_project/00_setup/run-config.md` | model, effort, run label, operator, machine, plan, permission mode, run type, feature, base run (every run); the run id is generated |
| `01_input/01_project/00_setup/secrets.env.example` | every secret the project needs (names only); copy to `.env` and fill the values there |
| `01_input/01_project/00_setup/tech-stack.md` | every platform, dependency and tool with exact versions |
| `01_input/01_project/00_setup/environments.md` | environments, settings, external services |
| `01_input/01_project/00_setup/pre-approved.md` | findings the human already decided (the agent records them without asking) |
| `01_input/01_project/01_requirements/user-stories.md` | user stories |
| `01_input/01_project/01_requirements/business-rules.md` | business rules, data fields, glossary |
| `01_input/01_project/01_requirements/scope.md` | in/out of scope, priorities, open questions with their answers |
| `01_input/01_project/01_requirements/acceptance-criteria.md` | the acceptance criteria, an input: the agent does not derive them |
| `01_input/01_project/01_requirements/e2e-scenarios.md` | the end-to-end scenarios, one test each, an input |
| `01_input/01_project/02_design/architecture.md` | components, constraints, interfaces |
| `01_input/01_project/02_design/security-requirements.md` | security level, authentication, personal data, project requirements |
| `01_input/01_project/02_design/quality-requirements.md` | non-functional requirements, thresholds, mutation scope, extra done criteria |
| `01_input/01_project/02_design/api-contract.md` | the fixed REST API (paths, fields, status codes, local test settings) that external checks rely on |
| `03_statistics/usage.md` | prices before the run (one row per model id, shape as in the file); nothing else |

Order: fill `01_requirements/` and `02_design/`, then `00_setup/`, then start the agent. It checks everything else in phase 0 and asks for whatever is missing.

## 2. Do not touch (change only when revising the template itself)

- `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, `Run_Guide.md`
- everything in `01_input/00_general/`:
  - `working-rules.md`, `phases.md`, `engineering-standards.md`
  - `quality/definition-of-done.md`, `quality/severity-scale.md`, `quality/test-strategy.md`, `quality/measurement-scope.md`
  - `security/security-baseline.md`
  - `skills/preflight/SKILL.md`, `skills/write-acceptance-tests/SKILL.md`, `skills/verify-release/SKILL.md`
- `03_statistics/metrics.md`, `03_statistics/run-log.template.json`, `03_statistics/tools/` (the post-run measuring, report and transcript-export scripts)

## 3. Written by the agent (read, do not edit)

- `02_output/README.md` and one README per component
- `02_output/docs/`: `00_preflight-report.md`, `00_input-manifest.sha256` (frozen once written), `00_progress.md`, `01_requirements-check.md`, `02_specification.md`, `02_contracts/`, `03_acceptance-manifest.sha256`, `03_test-strategy.md`, `06_verification-report.md`, `decisions-log.md`, `release-notes.md`
- `02_output/logs/`, all source code and tests in `02_output/`
- repository files required by ES-03 at the repository root: `.gitattributes`, `.gitignore`
- `03_statistics/run-log.json` (through `tools/stat.mjs` and by hand), `03_statistics/run-summary.md`
- written by the post-run session: `03_statistics/results/` (report, measurements, usage summary, commits, readable transcript) and `03_statistics/data/` (transcript backup, committed with the run)

Any change to sections 1 and 2 during a run is detected in phase 6 by comparing `00_input-manifest.sha256`.

## Rules for editing this template

- Start every Markdown file with `> Owner: … · Read in: … · Agent: …` (after the front matter in a `SKILL.md`; agent-written skeletons use `> Written in: … · Source: … · Agent: writes`) and add it to the right list above.
- State each rule once; link to it elsewhere. Write constraints ("Do not …"); procedures go in skills.
- One topic per file, no fixed length: split a file when it covers two topics or a reader needs only half of it. Versions appear only in `tech-stack.md`.

===== quality/definition-of-done.md
# Definition of Done

> Owner: QA lead · Read in: phases 6, 7 · Agent: read-only

Applies to every project; project additions are `DoD-Pnn` in `project/02_design/quality-requirements.md`.
Each item needs evidence in `docs/06_verification-report.md`.

| ID | Criterion | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| DoD-01 | The full test suite passes; frozen test hashes match the manifest | test report, hash check |
| DoD-02 | Format, lint, type check and static analysis report no errors | tool output |
| DoD-03 | The quality gate of `general/quality/measurement-scope.md` ("Quality gate") is met for each component, or the shortfall after the third survivor round is recorded with a decision | coverage and mutation reports with scope, raw and adjusted score, rounds |
| DoD-04 | Architecture constraints (`AR`) are checked automatically where possible; no dependency cycles | architecture test output |
| DoD-05 | No open Critical or High finding from the security review and scanners | `general/skills/verify-release` output |
| DoD-06 | Every component runs in its target environment and the core user flows work at runtime, not only in tests | runtime demonstration log |
| DoD-07 | Every AC traces to at least one test and one commit | traceability table |
| DoD-08 | Root and component READMEs (ES-06) work when followed from a clean checkout | clone log |
| DoD-09 | Release notes list everything a human must test manually | `docs/release-notes.md` |
| DoD-10 | Every decision has a resolution or is listed as pending review; inputs and protected files are unchanged | decisions log, `docs/00_input-manifest.sha256` check |
| DoD-11 | The evidence checks in `general/phases.md` hold | `general/phases.md`, "Evidence" |
===== quality/measurement-scope.md
# Measurement scope

> Owner: QA lead · Read in: phases 3, 5, 6 · Agent: read-only

Defines what test counts, coverage, mutation score and code size mean, so that figures from different runs compare. Record every figure in `run-log.json` → `codeMetrics` and in `docs/06_verification-report.md` with its scope, level and tool. The project selects paths and exclusions in `project/02_design/quality-requirements.md` ("Mutation scope"); this file never names them.

## Constraints

- Do not change a tool's scope, filters, exclusions or thresholds to improve a number. A change is a decision record.
- Do not report a figure without its scope, level and tool.
- Production code is the source a component ships. It excludes tests, generated code, the application entry point and anything listed under "Measurement exclusions" in `docs/03_test-strategy.md` with a reason. Decide the exclusions in phase 3, before any test is written; do not extend them later.
- Test code never counts towards coverage or mutation.

## Test counts

Per component and level (`unit`, `integration`, `acceptance`, `architecture`, `e2e`), passed and failed, from the runner's own report.

## Coverage

Line and branch, per component, as three figures: `unit` (unit tests only), `nonUnit` (integration, acceptance and end-to-end tests that exercise the component) and `all` (one merged report). The headline figure is `all`.

## Mutation score

- **Scope:** all production code of the component, narrowed only to the paths in `project/02_design/quality-requirements.md` "Mutation scope", which are the same in every run of the project (default: all production code). Do not narrow it by running only some tests or by excluding packages that are not listed there.
- **Tests:** the component's full automated suite, at every level it has, so the score does not depend on which level the agent ran. If that is infeasible, record the tests actually run and the reason in a decision record.
- **Record:** `{score, scoreAdjusted, scoreCovered, killed, equivalent, total, covered, scope, tests, tool, excluded}`. `score` (raw) = killed (timed-out counts as killed) ÷ all mutants the tool generated; a mutant no test reaches counts as survived. `scoreAdjusted` = (killed + equivalent) ÷ total, where `equivalent` is the number of survivors justified as equivalent. `scoreCovered` = killed ÷ mutants a test reaches.
- Do not remove equivalent mutants by hand. List every survivor you count as equivalent in `docs/03_test-strategy.md` with the class and method, the mutation and the reason it cannot change behaviour; a survivor without that entry is not equivalent. Always record the raw score next to the adjusted score.

===== 01_requirements/user-stories.md
# User stories

> Owner: Product owner · Read in: phases 1, 6 · Agent: read-only

## Format

- Stories: `US-nnn`, "As a … I want … so that …", plus in-scope and out-of-scope notes.
- Acceptance criteria are given in `acceptance-criteria.md` as `AC-nnn-nn` (Given/When/Then), one observable behaviour each, each citing its `US` and any `BR`; the agent does not derive them.
- Do not invent behaviour a story does not state; record the gap as an `OQ` in `scope.md`.

## Stories

Epic: as a conference organizer, I want participants to register online, so that registrations are collected and managed reliably.

### US-001 External participant registration

As an external participant, I want to register using the external participant form, so that I can attend the conference and the activities I select.
In scope: the external form (BR-01), selecting active options (BR-04). Out of scope: payment, accounts, editing a submitted registration.

### US-002 Student registration

As a student, I want to register using the student form, so that I can attend the conference and the activities available to students.
In scope: the student form (BR-01), selecting active options (BR-04). Out of scope: verifying student status externally, accounts.

### US-003 Configurable conference options

As an organizer, I want workshops, events, meals and other optional activities to be configurable, so that the system can be reused when the programme changes.
Out of scope: an administration UI for options.

### US-004 Registration confirmation

As a participant, I want a clear confirmation in the application after my registration is processed, so that I know it was received (BR-06).

### US-005 Reliable registration storage

As an organizer, I want every accepted registration stored reliably, so that none is lost and each can be recovered (BR-07).

### US-006 Participant email confirmation

As a participant, I want an email confirming my registration, so that I have a record of it.

### US-007 Organizer notification

As an organizer, I want an email when someone registers, containing the submitted data with the raw registration JSON attached, so that I can monitor incoming registrations.

### US-008 Registration export

As an organizer, I want to export the current registrations as an Excel workbook, so that I can process them outside the system (BR-08).
===== 01_requirements/business-rules.md
# Business rules

> Owner: Product owner · Read in: phases 1, 6 · Agent: read-only

## Rules

| ID | Rule |
|---|---|
| BR-01 | There are two registration types: external participant and student. Each has the fixed fields listed under Data; configuration never changes them. |
| BR-02 | Required fields are never empty; leading and trailing whitespace is not significant. |
| BR-03 | Email has a valid email format. Text accepts Unicode, including Slovenian characters (č, š, ž). |
| BR-04 | Options are grouped as workshops, events, meals and other activities. Only active options can be selected; unknown or inactive options are rejected. |
| BR-05 | Mandatory consents must be given and are never preselected. |
| BR-06 | The in-application confirmation is shown only after the registration was accepted. |
| BR-07 | An accepted registration is stored in the database and as a raw JSON copy on persistent storage. |
| BR-08 | Only organizers can obtain the registration list; it is not reachable without organizer access. |

## Data

| Form or entity | Fields (all required) |
|---|---|
| External participant | first name, last name, email, organization / institution |
| Student | first name, last name, email, study institution, study programme, student ID |
| Conference option | stable identifier, display name, category (workshop, event, meal, other), active or inactive |
| Consent | which consents exist and their wording: `OQ-02` |

## Glossary

- Participant: a person who registers, external or student.
- Organizer: conference staff who receive notifications and export registrations.
- Option: a selectable workshop, event, meal or other activity.
- Active option: an option currently offered for selection.
- Raw JSON copy: the registration exactly as accepted, stored as a file for backup.

> Owner: Product owner · Read in: phases 1, 6 · Agent: read-only

## In scope

- Registration forms for external participants and students (US-001, US-002)
- Configurable conference options (US-003)
- In-application confirmation, participant confirmation email, organizer notification email with the JSON attachment (US-004, US-006, US-007)
- Storage in the database plus a raw JSON copy (US-005)
- Excel export for organizers (US-008)
- Anti-automation protection of the registration form

## Out of scope

- Participant accounts and login
- Payment processing
- Editing or cancelling a submitted registration
- Verifying student status externally
- An administration UI or dashboard, including option configuration
- Integration with an identity provider

## Priorities

1. A registration is never lost: storage (BR-07) comes before any notification.
2. Security and privacy (`project/02_design/security-requirements.md`) come before convenience.
3. The participant flow (US-001 to US-006) comes before organizer features (US-007, US-008).

## Open questions

| ID | Question | Owner | Answer |
|---|---|---|---|
| OQ-01 | Are all options available to students, or are some only for external participants? | Product owner | Every option carries a configured list of registration types it is available to (default: both); the backend rejects an option that is not available to the registration type. |
| OQ-02 | Which mandatory consents exist, and what is their wording? | Product owner | Consents are part of the conference configuration (id, wording, mandatory). The shipped configuration has one mandatory consent `privacy`: "I agree that my personal data is processed for organizing the conference and that it is shared with the conference organizers." |
| OQ-03 | What happens when storage succeeds but an email fails? | Product owner | The registration stays accepted (HTTP 201, confirmation shown). Emails are sent only after the database row and the JSON copy exist; an email failure is logged with the registration id only, no personal data. |
| OQ-04 | How many options may a participant select per category? | Product owner | No limit per category; each option at most once per registration, duplicates are rejected. |
| OQ-05 | Is a second registration with the same email allowed? | Product owner | Allowed; each registration is stored separately and the export shows both. |
| OQ-06 | How long are registrations and JSON copies kept? | Product owner | Kept until the operator deletes them; no automatic deletion. The release notes tell the operator to delete the database rows and JSON copies no later than 12 months after the conference. |

The answers are the product owner's decisions and hold for every run of this project; the agent records no decision for them. A new question that arises later becomes a decision record as usual.

- Acceptance criteria are given in `acceptance-criteria.md` as `AC-nnn-nn` (Given/When/Then), one observable behaviour each, each citing its `US` and any `BR`; the agent does not derive them.
- Do not invent behaviour a story does not state; record the gap as an `OQ` in `scope.md`.

## Stories

Epic: as a conference organizer, I want participants to register online, so that registrations are collected and managed reliably.

### US-001 External participant registration

As an external participant, I want to register using the external participant form, so that I can attend the conference and the activities I select.
In scope: the external form (BR-01), selecting active options (BR-04). Out of scope: payment, accounts, editing a submitted registration.

### US-002 Student registration

As a student, I want to register using the student form, so that I can attend the conference and the activities available to students.
In scope: the student form (BR-01), selecting active options (BR-04). Out of scope: verifying student status externally, accounts.

### US-003 Configurable conference options

As an organizer, I want workshops, events, meals and other optional activities to be configurable, so that the system can be reused when the programme changes.
Out of scope: an administration UI for options.

### US-004 Registration confirmation

As a participant, I want a clear confirmation in the application after my registration is processed, so that I know it was received (BR-06).

### US-005 Reliable registration storage

As an organizer, I want every accepted registration stored reliably, so that none is lost and each can be recovered (BR-07).

### US-006 Participant email confirmation

As a participant, I want an email confirming my registration, so that I have a record of it.

### US-007 Organizer notification

As an organizer, I want an email when someone registers, containing the submitted data with the raw registration JSON attached, so that I can monitor incoming registrations.

### US-008 Registration export

As an organizer, I want to export the current registrations as an Excel workbook, so that I can process them outside the system (BR-08).
===== 01_requirements/business-rules.md
# Business rules

> Owner: Product owner · Read in: phases 1, 6 · Agent: read-only

## Rules

| ID | Rule |
|---|---|
| BR-01 | There are two registration types: external participant and student. Each has the fixed fields listed under Data; configuration never changes them. |
| BR-02 | Required fields are never empty; leading and trailing whitespace is not significant. |
| BR-03 | Email has a valid email format. Text accepts Unicode, including Slovenian characters (č, š, ž). |
| BR-04 | Options are grouped as workshops, events, meals and other activities. Only active options can be selected; unknown or inactive options are rejected. |
| BR-05 | Mandatory consents must be given and are never preselected. |
| BR-06 | The in-application confirmation is shown only after the registration was accepted. |
| BR-07 | An accepted registration is stored in the database and as a raw JSON copy on persistent storage. |
| BR-08 | Only organizers can obtain the registration list; it is not reachable without organizer access. |

## Data

| Form or entity | Fields (all required) |
|---|---|
| External participant | first name, last name, email, organization / institution |
| Student | first name, last name, email, study institution, study programme, student ID |
| Conference option | stable identifier, display name, category (workshop, event, meal, other), active or inactive |
| Consent | which consents exist and their wording: `OQ-02` |

## Glossary

- Participant: a person who registers, external or student.
- Organizer: conference staff who receive notifications and export registrations.
- Option: a selectable workshop, event, meal or other activity.
- Active option: an option currently offered for selection.
- Raw JSON copy: the registration exactly as accepted, stored as a file for backup.

> Owner: Product owner · Read in: phases 1, 6 · Agent: read-only

## In scope

- Registration forms for external participants and students (US-001, US-002)
- Configurable conference options (US-003)
- In-application confirmation, participant confirmation email, organizer notification email with the JSON attachment (US-004, US-006, US-007)
- Storage in the database plus a raw JSON copy (US-005)
- Excel export for organizers (US-008)
- Anti-automation protection of the registration form

## Out of scope

- Participant accounts and login
- Payment processing
- Editing or cancelling a submitted registration
- Verifying student status externally
- An administration UI or dashboard, including option configuration
- Integration with an identity provider

## Priorities

1. A registration is never lost: storage (BR-07) comes before any notification.
2. Security and privacy (`project/02_design/security-requirements.md`) come before convenience.
3. The participant flow (US-001 to US-006) comes before organizer features (US-007, US-008).

## Open questions

| ID | Question | Owner | Answer |
|---|---|---|---|
| OQ-01 | Are all options available to students, or are some only for external participants? | Product owner | Every option carries a configured list of registration types it is available to (default: both); the backend rejects an option that is not available to the registration type. |
| OQ-02 | Which mandatory consents exist, and what is their wording? | Product owner | Consents are part of the conference configuration (id, wording, mandatory). The shipped configuration has one mandatory consent `privacy`: "I agree that my personal data is processed for organizing the conference and that it is shared with the conference organizers." |
| OQ-03 | What happens when storage succeeds but an email fails? | Product owner | The registration stays accepted (HTTP 201, confirmation shown). Emails are sent only after the database row and the JSON copy exist; an email failure is logged with the registration id only, no personal data. |
| OQ-04 | How many options may a participant select per category? | Product owner | No limit per category; each option at most once per registration, duplicates are rejected. |
| OQ-05 | Is a second registration with the same email allowed? | Product owner | Allowed; each registration is stored separately and the export shows both. |
| OQ-06 | How long are registrations and JSON copies kept? | Product owner | Kept until the operator deletes them; no automatic deletion. The release notes tell the operator to delete the database rows and JSON copies no later than 12 months after the conference. |

The answers are the product owner's decisions and hold for every run of this project; the agent records no decision for them. A new question that arises later becomes a decision record as usual.

===== 01_requirements/acceptance-criteria.md
# Acceptance criteria

> Owner: Product owner · Read in: phases 1, 3, 6 · Agent: read-only

This list is an input, the same in every run of this project: the agent does not derive, add, merge or reword criteria. Each criterion states one observable behaviour (Given / When / Then) and cites its story and rules. "Rejected" always means: the API answers with an error status and field errors, no database row and no JSON copy are created, and no email is sent. The open questions are answered in `scope.md` (OQ-01 to OQ-06).

Common terms used below:

- *valid external submission*: registration type `EXTERNAL`; first name, last name, email, organization filled; every mandatory consent given; a reCAPTCHA token the verifier accepts; zero or more distinct active option ids available to the type.
- *valid student submission*: as above with type `STUDENT` and study institution, study programme and student ID instead of organization.

## US-001 External participant registration

| ID | Criterion | Refs |
|---|---|---|
| AC-001-01 | Given active options are configured, when a valid external submission is sent, then it is accepted (HTTP 201) and the response contains the new registration id. | BR-01, BR-04 |
| AC-001-02 | Given the external form, when any one required field (first name, last name, email, organization) is missing, empty or only whitespace, then the submission is rejected (HTTP 400) with an error for that field. | BR-01, BR-02 |
| AC-001-03 | Given a valid external submission whose text fields have leading and trailing spaces, when it is accepted, then the stored values have the spaces removed. | BR-02 |
| AC-001-04 | Given the external form, when the email does not have a valid email format, then the submission is rejected (HTTP 400) with an error for the email field. | BR-03 |
| AC-001-05 | Given the external form, when an option id is unknown, inactive or listed twice, then the submission is rejected (HTTP 400) with an error for the options. | BR-04, SR-04, OQ-04 |
| AC-001-06 | Given the external form, when a mandatory consent is not given, then the submission is rejected (HTTP 400) with an error for that consent. | BR-05, OQ-02 |
| AC-001-07 | Given the external form, when the reCAPTCHA token is missing or the verifier rejects it, then the submission is rejected (HTTP 400) and nothing is stored. | SR-01, scope (anti-automation) |
| AC-001-08 | Given the registration page, when the participant chooses "external participant", then the page shows exactly the external fields, the active options grouped as workshops, events, meals and other activities, and every consent checkbox unchecked. | BR-01, BR-04, BR-05 |

## US-002 Student registration

| ID | Criterion | Refs |
|---|---|---|
| AC-002-01 | Given active options are configured, when a valid student submission is sent, then it is accepted (HTTP 201) and the response contains the new registration id. | BR-01, BR-04 |
| AC-002-02 | Given the student form, when any one required field (first name, last name, email, study institution, study programme, student ID) is missing, empty or only whitespace, then the submission is rejected (HTTP 400) with an error for that field. | BR-01, BR-02 |
| AC-002-03 | Given the student form, when the email does not have a valid email format, then the submission is rejected (HTTP 400) with an error for the email field. | BR-03 |
| AC-002-04 | Given an active option configured as not available to students, when a student submission selects it, then the submission is rejected (HTTP 400) with an error for the options. | BR-04, OQ-01 |
| AC-002-05 | Given the student form, when a mandatory consent is not given, then the submission is rejected (HTTP 400) with an error for that consent. | BR-05, OQ-02 |
| AC-002-06 | Given the student form, when the reCAPTCHA token is missing or the verifier rejects it, then the submission is rejected (HTTP 400) and nothing is stored. | SR-01 |
| AC-002-07 | Given the registration page, when the participant chooses "student", then the page shows exactly the student fields and only the active options available to students, grouped by category, with every consent checkbox unchecked. | BR-01, BR-04, BR-05, OQ-01 |

## US-003 Configurable conference options

| ID | Criterion | Refs |
|---|---|---|
| AC-003-01 | Given a configuration with active and inactive options, when the form configuration is requested, then it lists only the active options, each with its identifier, display name, category and the registration types it is available to. | BR-04 |
| AC-003-02 | Given the backend is started with a different options configuration (an option added, one deactivated), when the form configuration is requested, then it reflects the new configuration, with no code change. | AR-04 |
| AC-003-03 | Given an options configuration that is invalid (duplicate identifier, unknown category, missing name), when the backend starts, then it refuses to start. | AR-04 |

## US-004 Registration confirmation

| ID | Criterion | Refs |
|---|---|---|
| AC-004-01 | Given a filled form, when the backend accepts the registration, then the page shows a confirmation with the participant's name and the selected options, and the form is no longer shown. | BR-06 |
| AC-004-02 | Given a filled form, when the backend rejects the registration with field errors, then no confirmation is shown, each error is shown next to its field, and the entered values remain. | BR-06, NFR-03 |
| AC-004-03 | Given a form with an empty required field or an invalid email, when the participant submits, then the page shows the field errors and sends no request to the backend. | NFR-03 |
| AC-004-04 | Given a filled form, when the backend fails or cannot be reached, then no confirmation is shown and a general error message without technical details is shown. | BR-06, SB-07 |

## US-005 Reliable registration storage

| ID | Criterion | Refs |
|---|---|---|
| AC-005-01 | Given a valid submission, when it is accepted, then the database holds one registration with the type, every submitted field, the selected options, each consent with the time it was given, and the time of registration. | BR-07 |
| AC-005-02 | Given a valid submission, when it is accepted, then a JSON copy named after the registration id exists in the JSON copy directory and contains the registration as accepted. | BR-07 |
| AC-005-03 | Given the JSON copy cannot be written, when a valid submission is sent, then the API answers with an error (not 201) and no registration is left in the database. | BR-07, AR-05 |
| AC-005-04 | Given a valid submission with Slovenian characters (č, š, ž, Č, Š, Ž) in the names and institution, when it is accepted, then the database row and the JSON copy contain the text unchanged. | BR-03, NFR-01 |

## US-006 Participant email confirmation

| ID | Criterion | Refs |
|---|---|---|
| AC-006-01 | Given a valid submission, when it is accepted, then one email is sent to the participant's address naming the conference, the participant and the selected options. | US-006 |
| AC-006-02 | Given a submission whose text fields contain line breaks, header-like text or HTML markup, when the confirmation email is sent, then the email has no additional headers or recipients and the markup appears only as literal text. | SR-05 |
| AC-006-03 | Given the mail server is unavailable, when a valid submission is sent, then the registration is still accepted (HTTP 201) and stored. | OQ-03, OQ-03 |

## US-007 Organizer notification

| ID | Criterion | Refs |
|---|---|---|
| AC-007-01 | Given organizer addresses are configured, when a registration is accepted, then each organizer address receives a notification email containing the submitted registration data. | US-007 |
| AC-007-02 | Given a registration is accepted, when the organizer notification is sent, then it has a JSON attachment whose content equals the stored JSON copy. | US-007, BR-07, SR-07 |

## US-008 Registration export

| ID | Criterion | Refs |
|---|---|---|
| AC-008-01 | Given stored registrations, when an organizer requests the export with valid organizer credentials, then the response is an Excel workbook (`.xlsx`) with one row per registration, containing its type, fields, selected options, consents and registration time. | BR-08 |
| AC-008-02 | Given stored registrations, when the export is requested without credentials or with wrong credentials, then it is refused (HTTP 401) and no registration data is returned. | BR-08, SB-02 |
| AC-008-03 | Given a registration with Slovenian characters, when the organizer exports, then the workbook cell contains the text unchanged. | NFR-01 |
| AC-008-04 | Given organizer HTTPS-only access is on, when the export is requested with valid credentials over plain HTTP from a client that is not on localhost, then it is refused and no registration data is returned. | SR-06 |

## Traceability

| Story | Criteria |
|---|---|
| US-001 | AC-001-01 … AC-001-08 |
| US-002 | AC-002-01 … AC-002-07 |
| US-003 | AC-003-01 … AC-003-03 |
| US-004 | AC-004-01 … AC-004-04 |
| US-005 | AC-005-01 … AC-005-04 |
| US-006 | AC-006-01 … AC-006-03 |
| US-007 | AC-007-01, AC-007-02 |
| US-008 | AC-008-01 … AC-008-04 |

Total: 35 criteria.

Requirements without their own criterion, covered in the specification and verified in phase 6: SR-03 rate and size limits, NFR-02 persistence across container recreation, NFR-04 health and readiness (runtime demonstration).
===== 01_requirements/e2e-scenarios.md
# End-to-end scenarios

> Owner: Product owner · Read in: phases 3, 6 · Agent: read-only

The end-to-end tests of this project: exactly one test per scenario below, run against the real local stack (`docker compose up`: frontend, backend, PostgreSQL, Mailpit) through the browser, and the same in every run of this project. The agent writes no other end-to-end test and no scenario is merged or split. Each scenario names the criteria it demonstrates; the acceptance tests (one or more per criterion) carry the detailed cases, so an end-to-end test checks the journey once and does not repeat them.

| ID | Scenario | Steps and observations | Covers |
|---|---|---|---|
| E2E-01 | External participant registers | Open the page, choose "external participant", fill the form with valid data, select at least one option per category, submit. The page shows the confirmation. The database holds the registration, the JSON copy exists, the participant email and the organizer email (with the JSON attachment) are in Mailpit. | AC-001-01, AC-001-08, AC-004-01, AC-005-01, AC-005-02, AC-006-01, AC-007-01, AC-007-02, DoD-P01 to DoD-P03 |
| E2E-02 | Student registers | As E2E-01 with "student": only the student fields and student-available options are shown; the registration is stored and both emails arrive. | AC-002-01, AC-002-07, AC-004-01, DoD-P01 to DoD-P03 |
| E2E-03 | Field errors are shown next to the fields | Submit the form with an empty required field and an invalid email: errors appear next to the fields and no request reaches the backend; then make the backend reject a submission (for example an unavailable option): the backend's field errors appear next to their fields and the entered values remain. | AC-004-02, AC-004-03, NFR-03 |
| E2E-04 | Slovenian characters survive the whole chain | Register with č, š, ž, Č, Š, Ž in the names and institution. The text is unchanged in the page confirmation, the database row, the JSON copy, both emails and the exported workbook. | AC-005-04, AC-008-03, NFR-01 |
| E2E-05 | Organizer exports registrations | Request the export with valid organizer credentials: a valid Excel workbook with one row per registration is downloaded. The same request without credentials is refused (HTTP 401) and returns no data. | AC-008-01, AC-008-02, DoD-P04 |

Not end-to-end tests (verified by runtime demonstration in phase 6): NFR-02 (data survives recreation of every container) and NFR-04 (health and readiness).

# Architecture

> Owner: Architect · Read in: phases 0, 2, 4, 6, 7 · Agent: read-only

## Components

Each component gets its own folder and README in `02_output/`. Versions come only from `tech-stack.md`; reference its ids, never repeat a version here.

```yaml
components:
  - name: backend
    type: api
    folder: 02_output/backend
    platform: java
    build: maven-wrapper
    bootstrap: Maven wrapper plus a hand-written pom.xml whose parent is org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-starter-parent; root package si.konferenca.registration
    commands:          # ES-05; filled in phase 0 if left empty
      build:
      test:
      check:
      run:
    depends_on: []
    deploys_as: container image (eclipse-temurin base, non-root)
  - name: frontend
    type: web-app
    folder: 02_output/frontend
    platform: node
    build: vite
    bootstrap: hand-written package.json with the exact tech-stack.md versions and a committed package-lock.json (no project generator)
    commands:
      build:
      test:
      check:
      run:
    depends_on: [backend]
    deploys_as: container image (static files served by nginx)
```

The local stack (both components, PostgreSQL, mail catcher) is started with `02_output/docker-compose.yml`.

## Constraints

Checkable rules the code must respect (layering, allowed dependencies, patterns). Checked automatically in phase 6 where the stack allows (DoD-04).

| ID | Constraint |
|---|---|
| AR-01 | The frontend talks to the backend only through the REST API under `/api`. |
| AR-02 | The backend's internal architecture is not prescribed: the agent declares and justifies it in `docs/02_specification.md` and then writes ArchUnit rules that check exactly that declaration. |
| AR-03 | No package cycles in the backend (ArchUnit slice check). |
| AR-04 | Conference options change through configuration only, without code changes and without changing the fixed participant fields (BR-01). The mechanism is decided in phase 2. |
| AR-05 | A success response is sent only after both the database row and the JSON copy are written (BR-06, BR-07). |
| AR-06 | The database schema changes only through Flyway migrations (ES-08). |
| AR-07 | The frontend contains no secret; the reCAPTCHA site key is its only key and comes from configuration. |
| AR-09 | The REST API under `/api` follows `api-contract.md` exactly: paths, methods, field names, status codes and the local test settings. |

## Interfaces

Every interface between components or with external systems is defined as a contract in `docs/02_contracts/` in phase 2. The REST API is fixed by `api-contract.md` (AR-09); its phase 2 contract describes exactly that API.

| Interface | Between | Style (e.g. REST, gRPC, events, file, UI) |
|---|---|---|
| Registration form | participant and frontend | UI |
| Options, registration, export | frontend or organizer and backend | REST (OpenAPI) |
| Registration storage | backend and PostgreSQL | SQL (JPA) |
| JSON copy | backend and persistent volume | file (JSON schema) |
| Conference options | configuration and backend | file or configuration (schema defined in phase 2) |
| Emails | backend and SMTP server | SMTP |
| Anti-automation | frontend, backend and Google reCAPTCHA | JavaScript widget, HTTPS verify call |

# Security requirements

> Owner: Security officer · Read in: phases 2, 6 · Agent: read-only

Adds to `general/security/security-baseline.md` (SB-01 … SB-14); do not repeat those here.

## Verification standard

| Component | Standard | Level | Reason if above the default |
|---|---|---|---|
| backend | OWASP ASVS 5.0 | Level 1 | |
| frontend | OWASP ASVS 5.0 | Level 1 | |

Level 1 is a deliberate choice: the only authentication is one organizer role for one export operation, and the personal data is contact and study data, not sensitive data. Where a requirement below is more specific than ASVS, it applies as well.

## Authentication and authorization

- Participants are anonymous; there are no participant accounts.
- One organizer role may export registrations (BR-08). The mechanism is decided in phase 2, using the organizer credentials from `secrets.env.example`; identity providers are out of scope.
- Everything else (options, registration) is public but protected by SR-01 and SR-03.

## Personal data

| Data item | Purpose | Retention | Shown/exported to |
|---|---|---|---|
| First and last name | identify the participant | `OQ-06` | organizers (email, export) |
| Email | confirmation and contact | `OQ-06` | participant, organizers |
| Organization / institution | attendance records | `OQ-06` | organizers |
| Study institution, programme, student ID | student registration | `OQ-06` | organizers |
| Selected options | plan workshops, events and meals | `OQ-06` | participant (confirmation), organizers |
| Consents given, with timestamp | proof of consent (SB-14) | `OQ-06` | organizers |

## Project requirements

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SR-01 | Every registration is protected by Google reCAPTCHA v2 and verified on the backend; the frontend check alone is never enough. |
| SR-02 | reCAPTCHA test mode is enabled only by environment configuration, never by default; production refuses to start with test mode on or with empty keys. |
| SR-03 | Every public `/api` endpoint (form configuration, registration, export) is rate limited per client, and request bodies have a size limit. |
| SR-04 | Option identifiers are checked against the active configured set (BR-04). |
| SR-05 | Email content is generated safely: user input cannot inject headers or markup. |
| SR-06 | Organizer credentials are never accepted over plain HTTP, except on localhost. |
| SR-07 | The export and the organizer email expose only registration data, never internal fields or other system data. |
| SR-08 | The reverse proxy in front of the backend never forwards a client-supplied `Host` header; it sets the upstream host itself. |

None.

# Quality requirements

> Owner: QA lead · Read in: phases 2, 6, 7 · Agent: read-only

## Thresholds

These thresholds are the **quality gate** of the project: the same in every run, per component (backend, frontend), over the scope and with the tests defined in `general/quality/measurement-scope.md`. The agent works until each component meets them, then stops adding tests for that component (rules and stop rule: "Quality gate" in `measurement-scope.md`). The rows below are read by `tools/build-report.mjs`; keep the format `>= <number> %`.

| Measure | Threshold |
|---|---|
| Line coverage (all levels together) | >= 95 % |
| Mutation score (adjusted) | >= 90 % |
| Branch coverage | record only |

## Mutation scope

The paths or packages whose code is mutated, the same in every run of this project (default: all production code of the component). Selection rule: validation, security, persistence and business-rule code. Rules: `general/quality/measurement-scope.md`.

| Component | Paths or packages | Exclusions and reason |
|---|---|---|
| backend | `si.konferenca.registration.**` (all production code under the root package, including validation, security, persistence, business-rule, mail and export code) | The `@SpringBootApplication` entry-point class (no logic); generated code. Nothing else may be excluded. |
| frontend | `src/**/*.{ts,tsx,js,jsx,vue}` (all production source of the frontend) | Test files, type-declaration files (`*.d.ts`), the bootstrap file that only mounts the app, generated code. Nothing else may be excluded. |

The scope is all production code of both components, so mutation scores are on the same basis in every run. It is the root package and the source folder, not a list of sub-packages, because the agent chooses the sub-packages in phase 2. Each component's full automated suite runs against it (`measurement-scope.md`, "Mutation score").

| ID | Criterion | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| DoD-P01 | Against the running local stack: one external and one student registration succeed. | runtime demonstration log |
| DoD-P02 | Each registration is in PostgreSQL and has its JSON copy. | database query, file listing |
| DoD-P03 | The participant email and the organizer email (with the JSON attachment) arrive in Mailpit. | Mailpit API output |
| DoD-P04 | The organizer downloads a valid Excel workbook; the same request without organizer access is refused. | response codes, opened workbook |

===== api-contract.md
# API contract

> Owner: Architect · Read in: phases 2, 3, 4, 6 · Agent: read-only

The REST API between the frontend or organizer and the backend is fixed by this file (AR-09): paths, methods, field names, status codes and the local test settings below are the same in every run of this project, so that external checks can use them. Everything not stated here (internal design, additional optional response fields, the OpenAPI document written in phase 2) is the agent's choice. The phase 2 contract in `docs/02_contracts/` must describe exactly this API.

## Local stack

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Backend base URL | `http://127.0.0.1:8080` (published by `02_output/docker-compose.yml`) |
| Mailpit web and API | `http://127.0.0.1:8025` |
| reCAPTCHA test mode | setting `CAPTCHA_TEST_MODE=true`; then the token `test-pass` is accepted and every other token is rejected |
| Rate limit | setting `RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE`: requests per minute per client and endpoint; the agent chooses the default |
| Organizer HTTPS-only access | setting `ORGANIZER_HTTPS_ONLY`; `false` is allowed only on local plain HTTP |

`docker-compose.yml` passes these three settings from the environment to the backend, so they can be changed with `docker compose up` without editing a file. Organizer credentials are `ORGANIZER_USERNAME` and `ORGANIZER_PASSWORD` from `.env`, sent with HTTP Basic authentication.

## Common rules

- Request and response bodies are JSON (`application/json; charset=utf-8`), except the export.
- Registration types are `EXTERNAL` and `STUDENT`; option categories are `WORKSHOP`, `EVENT`, `MEAL` and `OTHER`.
- Times are ISO 8601 with offset or `Z`.
- A rejected request (HTTP 400) has the body `{"errors": [{"field": "<name>", "message": "<text>"}]}`, one entry per invalid field. `field` is the request field's name as written in this file (for example `email`, `options`, `consents`, `captchaToken`); for a query parameter it is the parameter name.
- A request without valid organizer credentials on an organizer endpoint is answered with HTTP 401 and no registration data.
- A request over the rate limit (`RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE`) is answered with HTTP 429.

## Endpoints

### `GET /api/form-config` (public)

Response 200:

```json
{
  "options": [
    {"id": "ws-ai", "name": "AI workshop", "category": "WORKSHOP", "availableTo": ["EXTERNAL", "STUDENT"]}
  ],
  "consents": [
    {"id": "privacy", "text": "I agree that …", "mandatory": true}
  ],
  "captchaSiteKey": "…"
}
```

Lists only active options (AC-003-01).

### `POST /api/registrations` (public)

Request:

```json
{
  "type": "EXTERNAL",
  "firstName": "Ana",
  "lastName": "Novak",
  "email": "ana@example.org",
  "organization": "Example d.o.o.",
  "studyInstitution": null,
  "studyProgramme": null,
  "studentId": null,
  "options": ["ws-ai"],
  "consents": ["privacy"],
  "captchaToken": "test-pass"
}
```

- `organization` is required for `EXTERNAL`; `studyInstitution`, `studyProgramme` and `studentId` are required for `STUDENT`. Fields of the other type are ignored.
- `options` lists the selected option ids; `consents` lists the ids of the consents given.

Responses: 201 `{"id": "<registration id>"}`; 400 with field errors; any other error status when the registration could not be stored (AC-005-03).

### `GET /api/export` (organizer)

Response 200: an Excel workbook (`application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet`). The first sheet's first row holds these column headers, in this order, followed by one row per registration:

`id`, `type`, `firstName`, `lastName`, `email`, `organization`, `studyInstitution`, `studyProgramme`, `studentId`, `options`, `consents`, `registeredAt`

`options` and `consents` are the ids separated by `, `; a cell that does not apply to the registration's type is empty. Response 401 without valid organizer credentials.

Adds to `general/quality/` (definition of done, test strategy, severity scale); do not repeat those here.

## Non-functional requirements

| ID | Category (performance, availability, accessibility, localisation, usability, …) | Requirement | How it is checked |
|---|---|---|---|
| NFR-01 | Localisation | Names and other text with Slovenian characters (č, š, ž) survive the form, database, JSON copy, emails and Excel export unchanged. | an end-to-end test with such input |
| NFR-02 | Reliability | Stored registrations and JSON copies survive recreation of every container. | runtime demonstration: `docker compose down` then `up`, data still present |
| NFR-03 | Usability | The frontend validates fields before submission and shows the backend's field errors next to the fields. | component tests |
| NFR-04 | Availability | The backend reports health and readiness, and the containers use them in health checks. | runtime demonstration |

## Thresholds

These thresholds are the **quality gate** of the project: the same in every run, per component (backend, frontend), over the scope and with the tests defined in `general/quality/measurement-scope.md`. The agent works until each component meets them, then stops adding tests for that component (rules and stop rule: "Quality gate" in `measurement-scope.md`). The rows below are read by `tools/build-report.mjs`; keep the format `>= <number> %`.

| Measure | Threshold |
|---|---|
| Line coverage (all levels together) | >= 95 % |
| Mutation score (adjusted) | >= 90 % |
| Branch coverage | record only |

## Mutation scope

The paths or packages whose code is mutated, the same in every run of this project (default: all production code of the component). Selection rule: validation, security, persistence and business-rule code. Rules: `general/quality/measurement-scope.md`.

| Component | Paths or packages | Exclusions and reason |
|---|---|---|
| backend | `si.konferenca.registration.**` (all production code under the root package, including validation, security, persistence, business-rule, mail and export code) | The `@SpringBootApplication` entry-point class (no logic); generated code. Nothing else may be excluded. |
| frontend | `src/**/*.{ts,tsx,js,jsx,vue}` (all production source of the frontend) | Test files, type-declaration files (`*.d.ts`), the bootstrap file that only mounts the app, generated code. Nothing else may be excluded. |

The scope is all production code of both components, so mutation scores are on the same basis in every run. It is the root package and the source folder, not a list of sub-packages, because the agent chooses the sub-packages in phase 2. Each component's full automated suite runs against it (`measurement-scope.md`, "Mutation score").

## Additional done criteria

| ID | Criterion | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| DoD-P01 | Against the running local stack: one external and one student registration succeed. | runtime demonstration log |
| DoD-P02 | Each registration is in PostgreSQL and has its JSON copy. | database query, file listing |
| DoD-P03 | The participant email and the organizer email (with the JSON attachment) arrive in Mailpit. | Mailpit API output |
| DoD-P04 | The organizer downloads a valid Excel workbook; the same request without organizer access is refused. | response codes, opened workbook |
| DoD-P05 | The production reCAPTCHA code path is tested against a mocked verification endpoint, including a rejected token. | test report |

## Overrides

None.
===== api-contract.md
# API contract

> Owner: Architect · Read in: phases 2, 3, 4, 6 · Agent: read-only

The REST API between the frontend or organizer and the backend is fixed by this file (AR-09): paths, methods, field names, status codes and the local test settings below are the same in every run of this project, so that external checks can use them. Everything not stated here (internal design, additional optional response fields, the OpenAPI document written in phase 2) is the agent's choice. The phase 2 contract in `docs/02_contracts/` must describe exactly this API.

## Local stack

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Backend base URL | `http://127.0.0.1:8080` (published by `02_output/docker-compose.yml`) |
| Mailpit web and API | `http://127.0.0.1:8025` |
| reCAPTCHA test mode | setting `CAPTCHA_TEST_MODE=true`; then the token `test-pass` is accepted and every other token is rejected |
| Rate limit | setting `RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE`: requests per minute per client and endpoint; the agent chooses the default |
| Organizer HTTPS-only access | setting `ORGANIZER_HTTPS_ONLY`; `false` is allowed only on local plain HTTP |

`docker-compose.yml` passes these three settings from the environment to the backend, so they can be changed with `docker compose up` without editing a file. Organizer credentials are `ORGANIZER_USERNAME` and `ORGANIZER_PASSWORD` from `.env`, sent with HTTP Basic authentication.

## Common rules

- Request and response bodies are JSON (`application/json; charset=utf-8`), except the export.
- Registration types are `EXTERNAL` and `STUDENT`; option categories are `WORKSHOP`, `EVENT`, `MEAL` and `OTHER`.
- Times are ISO 8601 with offset or `Z`.
- A rejected request (HTTP 400) has the body `{"errors": [{"field": "<name>", "message": "<text>"}]}`, one entry per invalid field. `field` is the request field's name as written in this file (for example `email`, `options`, `consents`, `captchaToken`); for a query parameter it is the parameter name.
- A request without valid organizer credentials on an organizer endpoint is answered with HTTP 401 and no registration data.
- A request over the rate limit (`RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE`) is answered with HTTP 429.

## Endpoints

### `GET /api/form-config` (public)

Response 200:

```json
{
  "options": [
    {"id": "ws-ai", "name": "AI workshop", "category": "WORKSHOP", "availableTo": ["EXTERNAL", "STUDENT"]}
  ],
  "consents": [
    {"id": "privacy", "text": "I agree that …", "mandatory": true}
  ],
  "captchaSiteKey": "…"
}
```

Lists only active options (AC-003-01).

### `POST /api/registrations` (public)

Request:

```json
{
  "type": "EXTERNAL",
  "firstName": "Ana",
  "lastName": "Novak",
  "email": "ana@example.org",
  "organization": "Example d.o.o.",
  "studyInstitution": null,
  "studyProgramme": null,
  "studentId": null,
  "options": ["ws-ai"],
  "consents": ["privacy"],
  "captchaToken": "test-pass"
}
```

- `organization` is required for `EXTERNAL`; `studyInstitution`, `studyProgramme` and `studentId` are required for `STUDENT`. Fields of the other type are ignored.
- `options` lists the selected option ids; `consents` lists the ids of the consents given.

Responses: 201 `{"id": "<registration id>"}`; 400 with field errors; any other error status when the registration could not be stored (AC-005-03).

### `GET /api/export` (organizer)

Response 200: an Excel workbook (`application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet`). The first sheet's first row holds these column headers, in this order, followed by one row per registration:

`id`, `type`, `firstName`, `lastName`, `email`, `organization`, `studyInstitution`, `studyProgramme`, `studentId`, `options`, `consents`, `registeredAt`

`options` and `consents` are the ids separated by `, `; a cell that does not apply to the registration's type is empty. Response 401 without valid organizer credentials.

# Metrics

> Owner: Experiment lead · Read in: every phase and post-run · Agent: read-only

Experiment measurement only. Record observed values; never estimate. An unobservable value stays `null` with a `<field>Reason`.

Goal column: **↓** lower is better, **↑** higher is better, **=** should equal the stated value, **i** information for interpreting other numbers.

## Principles

- **Human waiting is not part of the result.** Agent time is wall time minus every wait for a human. A wait over one hour also lets the 1-hour prompt cache expire, and the call after it writes the whole context again; that rebuild is a cost of the wait, so `usage.costUsdExclWaits` removes it. Compare runs on agent time and `costUsdExclWaits`.
- **Record only what only you can see, and with the clock tool.** The agent records what happened (waits, loops, decisions, deviations, test and quality results). Timestamps come from `tools/stat.mjs`, never from memory or estimates. Everything that can be computed from the transcripts and git is computed after the run by `tools/build-report.mjs`, so the run spends no calls on it.
- **Make runs comparable.** Say what a number covers. Scope, level and tool of coverage, mutation score and code size are defined in `general/quality/measurement-scope.md`.

## 1. Agent, during the run → `run-log.json`

Phase 0, first action: `node 03_statistics/tools/stat.mjs init`. It creates `run-log.json` from the template, a unique `runId`, the start time and commit, the transcript path and the environment. It prints what it wrote.

| Field | When | How | Goal |
|---|---|---|---|
| `runId`, `model`, `effort`, `templateVersion`, `start`, `startCommit`, `transcript`, `environment` | phase 0 | written by `stat.mjs init` from `run-config.md`, git and the host | i |
| `phases[].start`, `phases[].end` | every phase boundary | `stat.mjs phase <n> start` and `stat.mjs phase <n> end`; a start also closes the previous phase, `phase 7 end` also sets `end` and `finalCommit` | ↓ agent time per phase |
| `humanInterventions[]` | every time the agent waits for the human or the human acts, including stops, restarts and installs | `stat.mjs wait start <cause> "<reason>" [decisionId]` when you ask or stop, `stat.mjs wait end` when work resumes. `cause`: `decision`, `environment`, `approval`, `session`, `other` | ↓ count and minutes; every minute here is excluded from agent time |
| `firstTestRun`, `finalTestRun` | first full run before fixes; last full run | edit the file: `passed`, `failed` and `byLevel` (`unit`, `integration`, `acceptance`, `architecture`, `e2e` counts) | first: ↓ failed (defects the first run found); final: ↑ passed, `failed` = 0 |

<project xmlns="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0"
         xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
         xsi:schemaLocation="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0 https://maven.apache.org/xsd/maven-4.0.0.xsd">
  <modelVersion>4.0.0</modelVersion>

  <parent>
    <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
    <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-parent</artifactId>
    <version>4.1.1</version>
    <relativePath/>
  </parent>

  <groupId>si.konferenca</groupId>
  <artifactId>registration-backend</artifactId>
  <version>1.0.0</version>
  <name>registration-backend</name>
  <description>Conference registration REST API</description>

  <properties>
    <java.version>21</java.version>
    <project.build.sourceEncoding>UTF-8</project.build.sourceEncoding>
    <!-- Overrides of Boot-managed versions (tech-stack.md) -->
    <tomcat.version>11.0.26</tomcat.version>
    <log4j2.version>2.26.1</log4j2.version>
    <commons-lang3.version>3.20.0</commons-lang3.version>

    <poi.version>5.5.1</poi.version>
    <archunit.version>1.3.2</archunit.version>

    <spotless.version>2.44.3</spotless.version>
    <spotbugs-plugin.version>4.10.4.1</spotbugs-plugin.version>
    <pmd-plugin.version>3.26.0</pmd-plugin.version>
    <jacoco.version>0.8.12</jacoco.version>
    <pitest.version>1.30.0</pitest.version>
    <pitest-junit5.version>1.2.3</pitest-junit5.version>
    <dependency-check.version>12.1.0</dependency-check.version>
  </properties>

  <dependencies>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
      <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-webmvc</artifactId>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
      <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-data-jpa</artifactId>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
      <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-validation</artifactId>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
      <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-mail</artifactId>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
      <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-actuator</artifactId>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
      <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-security</artifactId>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
      <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-flyway</artifactId>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>org.flywaydb</groupId>
      <artifactId>flyway-core</artifactId>
      <version>${flyway.version}</version>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>org.flywaydb</groupId>
      <artifactId>flyway-database-postgresql</artifactId>
      <version>${flyway.version}</version>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>org.postgresql</groupId>
      <artifactId>postgresql</artifactId>
      <version>${postgresql.version}</version>
      <scope>runtime</scope>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>org.apache.poi</groupId>
      <artifactId>poi-ooxml</artifactId>
      <version>${poi.version}</version>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>org.apache.tomcat.embed</groupId>
      <artifactId>tomcat-embed-core</artifactId>
      <version>${tomcat.version}</version>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>org.apache.logging.log4j</groupId>
      <artifactId>log4j-api</artifactId>
      <version>${log4j2.version}</version>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>org.apache.commons</groupId>
      <artifactId>commons-lang3</artifactId>
      <version>${commons-lang3.version}</version>
    </dependency>

    <dependency>
      <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
      <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-test</artifactId>
      <scope>test</scope>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
      <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-webmvc-test</artifactId>
      <scope>test</scope>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>org.testcontainers</groupId>
      <artifactId>testcontainers-junit-jupiter</artifactId>
      <version>${testcontainers.version}</version>
      <scope>test</scope>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>org.testcontainers</groupId>
      <artifactId>testcontainers-postgresql</artifactId>
      <version>${testcontainers.version}</version>
      <scope>test</scope>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>com.tngtech.archunit</groupId>
      <artifactId>archunit-junit5</artifactId>
      <version>${archunit.version}</version>
      <scope>test</scope>
    </dependency>
  </dependencies>

  <build>
    <plugins>
      <plugin>
        <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
        <artifactId>spring-boot-maven-plugin</artifactId>
        <version>4.1.1</version>
      </plugin>
      <plugin>
        <groupId>com.diffplug.spotless</groupId>
        <artifactId>spotless-maven-plugin</artifactId>
        <version>${spotless.version}</version>
        <configuration>
          <java>
            <googleJavaFormat/>
          </java>
        </configuration>
      </plugin>
      <plugin>
        <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
        <artifactId>maven-pmd-plugin</artifactId>
        <version>${pmd-plugin.version}</version>
        <configuration>
          <targetJdk>${java.version}</targetJdk>
          <printFailingErrors>true</printFailingErrors>
          <linkXRef>false</linkXRef>
        </configuration>
      </plugin>
      <plugin>
        <groupId>com.github.spotbugs</groupId>
        <artifactId>spotbugs-maven-plugin</artifactId>
        <version>${spotbugs-plugin.version}</version>
        <configuration>
          <effort>Max</effort>
          <threshold>Medium</threshold>
        </configuration>
      </plugin>
      <plugin>
        <groupId>org.jacoco</groupId>
        <artifactId>jacoco-maven-plugin</artifactId>
        <version>${jacoco.version}</version>
        <configuration>
          <excludes>
            <exclude>si/konferenca/registration/RegistrationApplication.class</exclude>
          </excludes>
        </configuration>
        <executions>
          <execution>
            <id>prepare-agent</id>
            <goals>
              <goal>prepare-agent</goal>
            </goals>
          </execution>
          <execution>
            <id>report</id>
            <phase>verify</phase>
            <goals>
              <goal>report</goal>
            </goals>
          </execution>
        </executions>
      </plugin>
      <plugin>
        <groupId>org.pitest</groupId>
        <artifactId>pitest-maven</artifactId>
        <version>${pitest.version}</version>
        <dependencies>
          <dependency>
            <groupId>org.pitest</groupId>
            <artifactId>pitest-junit5-plugin</artifactId>
            <version>${pitest-junit5.version}</version>
          </dependency>
        </dependencies>
        <configuration>
          <targetClasses>
            <param>si.konferenca.registration.*</param>
          </targetClasses>
          <excludedClasses>
            <param>si.konferenca.registration.RegistrationApplication</param>
          </excludedClasses>
          <outputFormats>
            <param>XML</param>
            <param>HTML</param>
          </outputFormats>
          <timestampedReports>false</timestampedReports>
        </configuration>
      </plugin>
      <plugin>
        <groupId>org.owasp</groupId>
        <artifactId>dependency-check-maven</artifactId>
        <version>${dependency-check.version}</version>
        <configuration>
          <nvdApiKeyEnvironmentVariable>NVD_API_KEY</nvdApiKeyEnvironmentVariable>
          <formats>
            <format>HTML</format>
            <format>JSON</format>
          </formats>
          <failBuildOnCVSS>11</failBuildOnCVSS>
        </configuration>
      </plugin>
    </plugins>
  </build>
</project>
