# Written in: phase 2 · Source: project/02_design/api-contract.md (AR-09) · Agent: writes
openapi: 3.1.0
info:
  title: Conference registration API
  version: 1.0.0
  description: >
    REST API between the frontend or organizer and the backend. Describes exactly the API fixed by
    project/02_design/api-contract.md. Every endpoint is rate limited per client and endpoint
    (RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE, HTTP 429) and request bodies are limited to 16 KiB (HTTP 413) (SR-03).
servers:
  - url: http://127.0.0.1:8080
    description: local stack (docker compose)
paths:
  /api/form-config:
    get:
      operationId: getFormConfig
      summary: Form configuration with the active options only (AC-003-01)
      security: []
      responses:
        "200":
          description: Active options, consents and the reCAPTCHA site key
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/FormConfig"
        "429":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/TooManyRequests"
  /api/registrations:
    post:
      operationId: createRegistration
      summary: Submit a registration (US-001, US-002, US-005)
      security: []
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              $ref: "#/components/schemas/RegistrationRequest"
      responses:
        "201":
          description: Accepted; the database row and the JSON copy exist (AR-05)
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/RegistrationCreated"
        "400":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/ValidationFailed"
        "413":
          description: Request body larger than the size limit
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/ErrorResponse"
        "429":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/TooManyRequests"
        "500":
          description: The registration could not be stored (AC-005-03); no row and no JSON copy remain
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/ErrorResponse"
  /api/export:
    get:
      operationId: exportRegistrations
      summary: Excel export of all registrations, organizer only (US-008, BR-08)
      security:
        - organizerBasic: []
      responses:
        "200":
          description: >
            Workbook whose first sheet's first row holds the headers id, type, firstName, lastName,
            email, organization, studyInstitution, studyProgramme, studentId, options, consents,
            registeredAt, followed by one row per registration. options and consents are ids joined
            with ", "; a cell that does not apply to the registration's type is empty.
          content:
            application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet:
              schema:
                type: string
                contentEncoding: binary
        "401":
          description: Missing or wrong organizer credentials; no registration data
        "403":
          description: >
            Organizer HTTPS-only access is on and the request came over plain HTTP from a client that
            is not on localhost (SR-06, AC-008-04); no registration data
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/ErrorResponse"
        "429":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/TooManyRequests"
components:
  securitySchemes:
    organizerBasic:
      type: http
      scheme: basic
      description: ORGANIZER_USERNAME and ORGANIZER_PASSWORD from the environment
  responses:
    ValidationFailed:
      description: Rejected; one entry per invalid field; nothing stored, no email sent
      content:
        application/json:
          schema:
            $ref: "#/components/schemas/ValidationErrors"
    TooManyRequests:
      description: More than RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE requests per minute from this client to this endpoint
      content:
        application/json:
          schema:
            $ref: "#/components/schemas/ErrorResponse"
  schemas:
    RegistrationType:
      type: string
      enum: [EXTERNAL, STUDENT]
    OptionCategory:
      type: string
      enum: [WORKSHOP, EVENT, MEAL, OTHER]
    FormOption:
      type: object
      required: [id, name, category, availableTo]
      properties:
        id:
          type: string
          examples: [ws-ai]
        name:
          type: string
          examples: [AI workshop]
        category:
          $ref: "#/components/schemas/OptionCategory"
        availableTo:
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: "#/components/schemas/RegistrationType"
    FormConsent:
      type: object
      required: [id, text, mandatory]
      properties:
        id:
          type: string
          examples: [privacy]
        text:
          type: string
        mandatory:
          type: boolean
    FormConfig:
      type: object
      required: [options, consents, captchaSiteKey]
      properties:
        options:
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: "#/components/schemas/FormOption"
        consents:
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: "#/components/schemas/FormConsent"
        captchaSiteKey:
          type: string
          description: reCAPTCHA v2 site key from configuration (AR-07); empty in test mode
        captchaTestMode:
          type: boolean
          description: Additional optional field; true when CAPTCHA_TEST_MODE is on
        conferenceName:
          type: string
          description: Additional optional field; the configured conference name
    RegistrationRequest:
      type: object
      required: [type, firstName, lastName, email, options, consents, captchaToken]
      properties:
        type:
          $ref: "#/components/schemas/RegistrationType"
        firstName:
          type: string
          maxLength: 200
        lastName:
          type: string
          maxLength: 200
        email:
          type: string
          maxLength: 254
        organization:
          type: [string, "null"]
          maxLength: 200
          description: Required for EXTERNAL; ignored for STUDENT
        studyInstitution:
          type: [string, "null"]
          maxLength: 200
          description: Required for STUDENT; ignored for EXTERNAL
        studyProgramme:
          type: [string, "null"]
          maxLength: 200
          description: Required for STUDENT; ignored for EXTERNAL
        studentId:
          type: [string, "null"]
          maxLength: 200
          description: Required for STUDENT; ignored for EXTERNAL
        options:
          type: array
          items:
            type: string
          description: Distinct ids of active options available to the type
        consents:
          type: array
          items:
            type: string
          description: Ids of the consents given; every mandatory consent must be listed
        captchaToken:
          type: string
          description: reCAPTCHA v2 response token; in test mode only "test-pass" is accepted
      examples:
        - type: EXTERNAL
          firstName: Ana
          lastName: Novak
          email: ana@example.org
          organization: Example d.o.o.
          studyInstitution: null
          studyProgramme: null
          studentId: null
          options: [ws-ai]
          consents: [privacy]
          captchaToken: test-pass
    RegistrationCreated:
      type: object
      required: [id]
      properties:
        id:
          type: string
          format: uuid
    FieldError:
      type: object
      required: [field, message]
      properties:
        field:
          type: string
          description: Request field name as in this document (email, options, consents, captchaToken, ...)
        message:
          type: string
    ValidationErrors:
      type: object
      required: [errors]
      properties:
        errors:
          type: array
          minItems: 1
          items:
            $ref: "#/components/schemas/FieldError"
    ErrorResponse:
      type: object
      required: [message]
      properties:
        message:
          type: string
          description: General message without internal details (SB-07)

|---|---|
| Options, registration, export (REST) | `openapi.yaml` |

| Conference options (configuration) | `conference-config.schema.json` |
| Emails (SMTP) | section "Emails" below |
| Anti-automation (reCAPTCHA) | section "reCAPTCHA" below |
| Registration form (UI) | section "Registration form" below |

## Emails

Sent by the backend over SMTP (`SMTP_HOST`, `SMTP_PORT`, `SMTP_TLS`, optional `SMTP_USERNAME` / `SMTP_PASSWORD`) only after the database row and the JSON copy exist (OQ-03). A send failure is logged with the registration id only and does not change the HTTP 201 answer.

| Mail | To | From | Subject | Body | Attachment |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Participant confirmation (US-006) | the participant's validated email, one recipient | `MAIL_FROM` | `Registration confirmed: <conference name>` | `text/plain; charset=UTF-8`: conference name, participant first and last name, registration id, selected option names (or "none") | none |
| Organizer notification (US-007) | each address in `ORGANIZER_EMAILS`, one message per address | `MAIL_FROM` | `New registration: <conference name>` | `text/plain; charset=UTF-8`: registration id, type, every registration field (`label: value`), option ids and names, consent ids with time, registration time | `registration-<id>.json`, `application/json`, the bytes of the stored JSON copy |

Safety (SR-05, SR-07): headers contain no participant input except the recipient address, which passed the email rule (D-09, no whitespace or control characters) and is set through the mail API, never by string concatenation; bodies are plain text, so markup is shown literally; the organizer mail and attachment carry only registration fields.

## reCAPTCHA

| Mode | Setting | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| Production | `CAPTCHA_TEST_MODE=false` (default), `RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY`, `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY` | Backend posts `secret` and `response` (form-encoded) to `RECAPTCHA_VERIFY_URL` (default `https://www.google.com/recaptcha/api/siteverify`) with a 5 s timeout; accepts only `{"success": true}`. Any other answer, error or timeout rejects the token. |
| Test | `CAPTCHA_TEST_MODE=true` | No network call; `test-pass` is accepted, every other token rejected (api-contract). |

Start-up guard (SR-02): with `APP_ENVIRONMENT=production`, the backend refuses to start when test mode is on or either key is empty. Frontend: `captchaSiteKey` (and `captchaTestMode`) come from `GET /api/form-config`. With a site key the frontend loads the Google v2 widget and sends its token; in test mode it shows a "test mode" checkbox that yields the token `test-pass`.

## Registration form

Single page at `/` served by the frontend; it calls only `/api/*` (AR-01).

1. On load: `GET /api/form-config`. On failure: a general error, no form.
2. Choice of registration type: radio buttons "External participant" and "Student"; no type preselected, no fields before a choice.
3. Fields: external: first name, last name, email, organization / institution. Student: first name, last name, email, study institution, study programme, student ID. Each field has a label and an error slot right after it.
4. Options: active options available to the chosen type, as checkboxes grouped under the headings Workshops, Events, Meals, Other activities (a group without options is not shown). None preselected.
5. Consents: one checkbox per configured consent with its text, never preselected (BR-05).
6. reCAPTCHA widget, then the submit button.
7. Before sending: required fields (after trimming), email format (D-09), length (D-08), mandatory consents and the captcha token are checked; any error is shown next to its field and no request is sent (AC-004-03).
8. 201: the form is replaced by a confirmation with the participant's name and the selected option names (AC-004-01).
9. 400: each `errors[].field` message is shown next to its field (unknown fields as a general message); entered values stay (AC-004-02).
10. Any other status or a network error: a general message "Registration could not be completed. Please try again later." with no technical detail; values stay (AC-004-04).

Accessible names (used by the tests): field labels "First name", "Last name", "Email", "Organization / institution", "Study institution", "Study programme", "Student ID"; group headings "Workshops", "Events", "Meals", "Other activities"; button "Register"; error elements have `role="alert"` and are linked with `aria-describedby`.

# Specification

> Written in: phase 2 · Source: `project/01_requirements/*`, `project/02_design/*`, `project/00_setup/tech-stack.md`, `environments.md`, `general/security/*` · Agent: writes

Contracts: [`02_contracts/`](02_contracts/) (`openapi.yaml`, `database-schema.sql`, `registration-copy.schema.json`, `conference-config.schema.json`, `interfaces.md`).

## 1. Components

| Component | Folder | Runs as | Talks to |
|---|---|---|---|
| backend | `02_output/backend` | Spring Boot 4.1.1 jar in an `eclipse-temurin` JRE image, non-root user, port 8080 | PostgreSQL (JPA), SMTP, reCAPTCHA verify URL, JSON copy volume |
| frontend | `02_output/frontend` | React 19 single page built by Vite, served by `nginx` as a non-root user, port 8080 in the container | backend only via `/api` (AR-01); nginx proxies `/api/` to the backend with a fixed upstream `Host` (SR-08) |
| local stack | `02_output/docker-compose.yml` | `postgres`, `mailpit`, `backend`, `frontend`; ports bound to 127.0.0.1: backend 8080, frontend 8081, Mailpit 8025 | named volumes `pgdata`, `jsoncopies` (NFR-02) |

## 2. Backend architecture (AR-02 declaration)

Ports and adapters with three layers under `si.konferenca.registration`. Chosen because the core rule set (validation, option availability, consents, storage order) must be testable without Spring, PostgreSQL, SMTP or Google, and because each external system (database, file, mail, reCAPTCHA, Excel) is replaceable behind one interface.

| Package | Contents | May depend on |
|---|---|---|
| `domain` | `Registration`, `RegistrationType`, `ConferenceOption`, `OptionCategory`, `Consent`, `ConferenceConfig`, `RegistrationSubmission`, `RegistrationValidator`, `FieldError`, `ValidationException` | JDK only (no Spring, Jakarta, Jackson, POI) |
| `application` | `RegistrationService` (use case), `ExportService`, ports `RegistrationRepository`, `JsonCopyStore`, `CaptchaVerifier`, `RegistrationNotifier`, `RegistrationExporter`, `Clock` use | `domain`, Spring transaction annotations |
| `adapter.web` | controllers, request/response DTOs, `ApiExceptionHandler`, `RateLimitFilter`, `BodySizeLimitFilter`, `OrganizerTransportFilter` | `application`, `domain` |
| `adapter.persistence` | JPA entities, Spring Data repositories, `JpaRegistrationRepository` | `application`, `domain` |
| `adapter.jsoncopy` | `FileJsonCopyStore` | `application`, `domain` |
| `adapter.mail` | `MailRegistrationNotifier` | `application`, `domain` |
| `adapter.captcha` | `TestModeCaptchaVerifier`, `RecaptchaHttpVerifier` | `application`, `domain` |
| `adapter.export` | `ExcelRegistrationExporter` (POI) | `application`, `domain` |
| `config` | `@ConfigurationProperties`, `ConferenceConfigLoader`, `SecurityConfig`, `ProductionGuard`, bean wiring | everything above |

ArchUnit rules (DoD-04), test `ArchitectureTest`:

- A1 `domain` depends on no other package of the application and on no `org.springframework..`, `jakarta..`, `com.fasterxml..`, `tools.jackson..`, `org.apache.poi..` class.
- A2 `application` depends only on `domain` (and JDK, `org.springframework.transaction..`, `org.slf4j..`).
- A3 no adapter package depends on another adapter package or on `config`.
- A4 no package cycles between the slices `si.konferenca.registration.(*)..` and `adapter.(*)` (AR-03).
- A5 only `adapter.persistence` uses `jakarta.persistence..`; only `adapter.export` uses `org.apache.poi..`; only `adapter.mail` uses `org.springframework.mail..` / `jakarta.mail..`.

## 3. Behaviour

### 3.1 Conference configuration (US-003, AR-04)

- Source: JSON file at `CONFERENCE_CONFIG_PATH` (schema `conference-config.schema.json`); default `classpath:conference.json` allowed only outside production. The shipped file has two options per category, one student-only and one external-only option, one inactive option and the mandatory consent `privacy` with the OQ-02 wording.
- Loaded once at start by `ConferenceConfigLoader`. The backend refuses to start (context failure, non-zero exit) when the file is missing, not valid JSON, has unknown properties, a missing or blank `name`, `id` or consent `text`, an unknown category or registration type, or a duplicate option or consent id (AC-003-03). `active` defaults to `true`, `availableTo` to both types.
- `GET /api/form-config` returns the active options in file order, each with `id`, `name`, `category`, `availableTo`; all consents; `captchaSiteKey`; `captchaTestMode`; `conferenceName` (AC-003-01). A changed file takes effect on the next start without code change (AC-003-02).

### 3.2 Registration (US-001, US-002, US-005)

`POST /api/registrations` → `RegistrationService.register(submission)`:

1. Parse the body as a map of nullable strings and string lists; a non-JSON body, a wrong JSON type or an unknown `type` value is a field error (`type`, or `body` for an unreadable body).
2. Trim every text field (BR-02). Fields of the other type are ignored and stored as `null`.
3. Validate, collecting all errors (one entry per field): required fields non-empty (`firstName`, `lastName`, `email`, plus `organization` or `studyInstitution`, `studyProgramme`, `studentId`); length ≤ 200, email ≤ 254 (D-08); email format (D-09); `options`: every id known, active, available to the type, not listed twice, otherwise one `options` error (SR-04, OQ-01, OQ-04); `consents`: every mandatory consent present (one `consents` error), unknown consent ids rejected; `captchaToken` present.
4. Only when step 3 found no error: verify the token with `CaptchaVerifier`; rejected → `captchaToken` error (SR-01). Errors → HTTP 400 `{"errors":[…]}`, nothing stored, no mail (AC-001-02 … 07, AC-002-02 … 06).
5. In one database transaction: insert the registration, its options and consents (each consent with `givenAt` = registration time), flush; write the JSON copy (`<JSON_COPY_DIR>/<id>.json`, written to a temp file in the same directory, then atomically moved). If the write fails, the transaction rolls back and the API answers 500 with a general message (AC-005-03, AR-05). If the commit fails after the file was written, the file is deleted.
6. After commit: send the participant mail, then the organizer mails (attachment = the JSON copy bytes). Each failure is caught and logged as `mail failed for registration <id>` (OQ-03, AC-006-03).
7. Answer 201 `{"id": "<uuid>"}`.

Registration id: random UUID; time: `Clock` in UTC, stored as `timestamptz`, serialised ISO 8601 with `Z`. Repeat emails are allowed (OQ-05). Text is stored and written as UTF-8 unchanged (AC-005-04, NFR-01): the database uses UTF-8, the JSON copy is written with Jackson as UTF-8.

### 3.3 Emails (US-006, US-007)

As `02_contracts/interfaces.md`, "Emails". SMTP connection and read timeouts 5 s, so an unavailable server does not hold the response.

### 3.4 Export (US-008)

`GET /api/export` with HTTP Basic: the single in-memory user `ORGANIZER_USERNAME` with role `ORGANIZER`; the password from `ORGANIZER_PASSWORD` is BCrypt-hashed at start and only the hash is kept (SB-03). ### 3.1 Conference configuration (US-003, AR-04)

### 3.2 Registration (US-001, US-002, US-005)

2. Trim every text field (BR-02). Fields of the other type are ignored and stored as `null`.
3. 4. Only when step 3 found no error: verify the token with `CaptchaVerifier`; rejected → `captchaToken` error (SR-01). Errors → HTTP 400 `{"errors":[…]}`, nothing stored, no mail (AC-001-02 … 07, AC-002-02 … 06).
5. In one database transaction: insert the registration, its options and consents (each consent with `givenAt` = registration time), flush; write the JSON copy (`<JSON_COPY_DIR>/<id>.json`, written to a temp file in the same directory, then atomically moved). If the write fails, the transaction rolls back and the API answers 500 with a general message (AC-005-03, AR-05). If the commit fails after the file was written, the file is deleted.

7. Answer 201 `{"id": "<uuid>"}`.

Registration id: random UUID; time: `Clock` in UTC, stored as `timestamptz`, serialised ISO 8601 with `Z`. Repeat emails are allowed (OQ-05). Text is stored and written as UTF-8 unchanged (AC-005-04, NFR-01): the database uses UTF-8, the JSON copy is written with Jackson as UTF-8.

# Specification

> Written in: phase 2 · Source: `project/01_requirements/*`, `project/02_design/*`, `project/00_setup/tech-stack.md`, `environments.md`, `general/security/*` · Agent: writes

Contracts: [`02_contracts/`](02_contracts/) (`openapi.yaml`, `database-schema.sql`, `registration-copy.schema.json`, `conference-config.schema.json`, `interfaces.md`).

## 1. Components

| Component | Folder | Runs as | Talks to |
|---|---|---|---|
| backend | `02_output/backend` | Spring Boot 4.1.1 jar in an `eclipse-temurin` JRE image, non-root user, port 8080 | PostgreSQL (JPA), SMTP, reCAPTCHA verify URL, JSON copy volume |
| frontend | `02_output/frontend` | React 19 single page built by Vite, served by `nginx` as a non-root user, port 8080 in the container | backend only via `/api` (AR-01); nginx proxies `/api/` to the backend with a fixed upstream `Host` (SR-08) |
| local stack | `02_output/docker-compose.yml` | `postgres`, `mailpit`, `backend`, `frontend`; ports bound to 127.0.0.1: backend 8080, frontend 8081, Mailpit 8025 | named volumes `pgdata`, `jsoncopies` (NFR-02) |

## 2. Backend architecture (AR-02 declaration)

Ports and adapters with three layers under `si.konferenca.registration`. Chosen because the core rule set (validation, option availability, consents, storage order) must be testable without Spring, PostgreSQL, SMTP or Google, and because each external system (database, file, mail, reCAPTCHA, Excel) is replaceable behind one interface.

| Package | Contents | May depend on |
|---|---|---|
| `domain` | `Registration`, `RegistrationType`, `ConferenceOption`, `OptionCategory`, `Consent`, `ConferenceConfig`, `RegistrationSubmission`, `RegistrationValidator`, `FieldError`, `ValidationException` | JDK only (no Spring, Jakarta, Jackson, POI) |
| `application` | `RegistrationService` (use case), `ExportService`, ports `RegistrationRepository`, `JsonCopyStore`, `CaptchaVerifier`, `RegistrationNotifier`, `RegistrationExporter`, `Clock` use | `domain`, Spring transaction annotations |
| `adapter.web` | controllers, request/response DTOs, `ApiExceptionHandler`, `RateLimitFilter`, `BodySizeLimitFilter`, `OrganizerTransportFilter` | `application`, `domain` |
| `adapter.persistence` | JPA entities, Spring Data repositories, `JpaRegistrationRepository` | `application`, `domain` |
| `adapter.jsoncopy` | `FileJsonCopyStore` | `application`, `domain` |
| `adapter.mail` | `MailRegistrationNotifier` | `application`, `domain` |
| `adapter.captcha` | `TestModeCaptchaVerifier`, `RecaptchaHttpVerifier` | `application`, `domain` |
| `adapter.export` | `ExcelRegistrationExporter` (POI) | `application`, `domain` |
| `config` | `@ConfigurationProperties`, `ConferenceConfigLoader`, `SecurityConfig`, `ProductionGuard`, bean wiring | everything above |

ArchUnit rules (DoD-04), test `ArchitectureTest`:

- A1 `domain` depends on no other package of the application and on no `org.springframework..`, `jakarta..`, `com.fasterxml..`, `tools.jackson..`, `org.apache.poi..` class.
- A2 `application` depends only on `domain` (and JDK, `org.springframework.transaction..`, `org.slf4j..`).
- A3 no adapter package depends on another adapter package or on `config`.
- A4 no package cycles between the slices `si.konferenca.registration.(*)..` and `adapter.(*)` (AR-03).
- A5 only `adapter.persistence` uses `jakarta.persistence..`; only `adapter.export` uses `org.apache.poi..`; only `adapter.mail` uses `org.springframework.mail..` / `jakarta.mail..`.

## 3. Behaviour

### 3.1 Conference configuration (US-003, AR-04)

- Source: JSON file at `CONFERENCE_CONFIG_PATH` (schema `conference-config.schema.json`); default `classpath:conference.json` allowed only outside production. The shipped file has two options per category, one student-only and one external-only option, one inactive option and the mandatory consent `privacy` with the OQ-02 wording.
- Loaded once at start by `ConferenceConfigLoader`. The backend refuses to start (context failure, non-zero exit) when the file is missing, not valid JSON, has unknown properties, a missing or blank `name`, `id` or consent `text`, an unknown category or registration type, or a duplicate option or consent id (AC-003-03). `active` defaults to `true`, `availableTo` to both types.
- `GET /api/form-config` returns the active options in file order, each with `id`, `name`, `category`, `availableTo`; all consents; `captchaSiteKey`; `captchaTestMode`; `conferenceName` (AC-003-01). A changed file takes effect on the next start without code change (AC-003-02).

### 3.2 Registration (US-001, US-002, US-005)

`POST /api/registrations` → `RegistrationService.register(submission)`:

1. Parse the body as a map of nullable strings and string lists; a non-JSON body, a wrong JSON type or an unknown `type` value is a field error (`type`, or `body` for an unreadable body).
2. Trim every text field (BR-02). Fields of the other type are ignored and stored as `null`.
3. Validate, collecting all errors (one entry per field): required fields non-empty (`firstName`, `lastName`, `email`, plus `organization` or `studyInstitution`, `studyProgramme`, `studentId`); length ≤ 200, email ≤ 254 (D-08); email format (D-09); `options`: every id known, active, available to the type, not listed twice, otherwise one `options` error (SR-04, OQ-01, OQ-04); `consents`: every mandatory consent present (one `consents` error), unknown consent ids rejected; `captchaToken` present.
4. Only when step 3 found no error: verify the token with `CaptchaVerifier`; rejected → `captchaToken` error (SR-01). Errors → HTTP 400 `{"errors":[…]}`, nothing stored, no mail (AC-001-02 … 07, AC-002-02 … 06).
5. In one database transaction: insert the registration, its options and consents (each consent with `givenAt` = registration time), flush; write the JSON copy (`<JSON_COPY_DIR>/<id>.json`, written to a temp file in the same directory, then atomically moved). If the write fails, the transaction rolls back and the API answers 500 with a general message (AC-005-03, AR-05). If the commit fails after the file was written, the file is deleted.
6. After commit: send the participant mail, then the organizer mails (attachment = the JSON copy bytes). Each failure is caught and logged as `mail failed for registration <id>` (OQ-03, AC-006-03).
7. Answer 201 `{"id": "<uuid>"}`.

Registration id: random UUID; time: `Clock` in UTC, stored as `timestamptz`, serialised ISO 8601 with `Z`. Repeat emails are allowed (OQ-05). Text is stored and written as UTF-8 unchanged (AC-005-04, NFR-01): the database uses UTF-8, the JSON copy is written with Jackson as UTF-8.

### 3.3 Emails (US-006, US-007)

As `02_contracts/interfaces.md`, "Emails". SMTP connection and read timeouts 5 s, so an unavailable server does not hold the response.

### 3.4 Export (US-008)

`GET /api/export` with HTTP Basic: the single in-memory user `ORGANIZER_USERNAME` with role `ORGANIZER`; the password from `ORGANIZER_PASSWORD` is BCrypt-hashed at start and only the hash is kept (SB-03). Wrong or missing credentials → 401, empty body, `WWW-Authenticate: Basic` (AC-008-02). Then `OrganizerTransportFilter` (SR-06, AC-008-04): when `ORGANIZER_HTTPS_ONLY=true` (default) and the request is not secure and the client address is not a loopback address → 403 with a general message, no data. Behind the production proxy the scheme and client address come from `X-Forwarded-Proto` / `X-Forwarded-For` as resolved by Tomcat's remote IP handling for trusted internal proxies (`server.forward-headers-strategy=native`).

Workbook: one sheet `registrations`, row 1 the 12 headers of `api-contract.md` in order, then one row per registration ordered by `registeredAt`, `id`; every cell a string cell (no formulas, so no formula injection); `options` and `consents` ids joined by `, `; cells of the other type empty (AC-008-01, AC-008-03). Content type `application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet`, `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="registrations.xlsx"`. Only registration fields are exported (SR-07).

### 3.5 Errors, limits and headers

- `ApiExceptionHandler`: validation → 400 with field errors; unreadable body → 400 field `body`; body too large → 413; anything else → 500 `{"message":"The request could not be processed."}`. No stack traces, exception messages or personal data in responses or logs (SB-07, ES-07); the log line carries the registration id or the exception class only.
- Rate limit (SR-03, SB-06): `RateLimitFilter` on every `/api/**` request, fixed one-minute window per client address and endpoint path, limit `RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE` (default 60, D-10); over the limit → 429 `{"message":"Too many requests. Please try again later."}` with `Retry-After`. It runs before authentication, so failed logins are limited too.
- Body size (SR-03): `BodySizeLimitFilter` rejects a body over 16 KiB (`REQUEST_MAX_BYTES`, default 16384) with 413, by `Content-Length` and by counting streamed bytes.
- Headers (SB-10): Spring Security defaults (`X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `Cache-Control: no-store`) plus `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'` and `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` on the API. nginx adds for the frontend: CSP `default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' https://www.google.com/recaptcha/ https://www.gstatic.com/recaptcha/; frame-src https://www.google.com/recaptcha/ https://recaptcha.google.com/recaptcha/; img-src 'self' data:; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; connect-src 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'self'`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`.
- CSRF is disabled and sessions are stateless: the API uses no cookies; the only credential is HTTP Basic on one GET.
- CORS: only `ALLOWED_ORIGIN` (unset by default, set only in local development with the Vite dev server).
- Health (NFR-04, ES-09): `/actuator/health`, `/actuator/health/liveness`, `/actuator/health/readiness` public, no details; every other actuator endpoint off. Readiness includes the database. Compose health checks use readiness.

### 3.6 Frontend

As `02_contracts/interfaces.md`, "Registration form". Modules: `api.ts` (fetch wrappers, the only place that knows URLs), `validation.ts` (client rules mirroring 3.2 step 3), `RegistrationForm.tsx`, `OptionGroups.tsx`, `Captcha.tsx`, `Confirmation.tsx`, `App.tsx`. The frontend holds no secret; the site key comes from `/api/form-config` (AR-07). All text is rendered through React (escaped, SB-05).

## 4. Configuration (ES-01)

| Setting | Default | Allowed default in | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `APP_ENVIRONMENT` | `local` | local, test | `production` enables `ProductionGuard` |
| `DB_URL`, `DB_USER`, `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` | `jdbc:postgresql://localhost:5432/registration`, `registration`, none | local, test (password: none anywhere) | database |
| `SMTP_HOST`, `SMTP_PORT`, `SMTP_TLS`, `SMTP_USERNAME`, `SMTP_PASSWORD` | `localhost`, `1025`, `false`, empty, empty | local, test | mail |
| `MAIL_FROM` | `registration@konferenca.local` | all | sender |
| `ORGANIZER_EMAILS` | none | — | organizer recipients |
| `ORGANIZER_USERNAME`, `ORGANIZER_PASSWORD` | none | — | export login; start fails if empty |
| `CONFERENCE_CONFIG_PATH` | `classpath:conference.json` | local, test | options and consents (conference name is in the file) |
| `JSON_COPY_DIR` | `./data/json-copies` (compose: `/data/json-copies` on volume `jsoncopies`) | all | JSON copies |
| `CAPTCHA_TEST_MODE` | `false` | all (on only in test and local) | test mode |
| `RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY`, `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY` | empty | local, test | reCAPTCHA keys |
| `RECAPTCHA_VERIFY_URL` | `https://www.google.com/recaptcha/api/siteverify` | all | verify endpoint (mocked in tests, DoD-P05) |
| `ORGANIZER_HTTPS_ONLY` | `true` (compose local: `false`, D-11) | all | SR-06 |
| `ALLOWED_ORIGIN` | empty | local | CORS |
| `RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE` | `60` (D-10) | all | SR-03 |
| `REQUEST_MAX_BYTES` | `16384` | all | SR-03 |

`ProductionGuard` (SR-02, `environments.md`): with `APP_ENVIRONMENT=production` the backend refuses to start when `CAPTCHA_TEST_MODE=true`, either reCAPTCHA key is empty, `ORGANIZER_HTTPS_ONLY=false`, `ALLOWED_ORIGIN` is set, or `DB_URL`, `SMTP_HOST` or `CONFERENCE_CONFIG_PATH` is left at its default.

- Backend image: build stage `eclipse-temurin:21.0.10_7-jdk-alpine` (D-12) runs `./mvnw -DskipTests package`; runtime `eclipse-temurin:21.0.10_7-jre-alpine`, user `app` (uid 10001), `/data/json-copies` owned by it (SB-11); `HEALTHCHECK` on readiness.

- Timestamp: $T
- Phase: 2
- Type: non-blocking
- Trigger: \`api-contract.md\` leaves the \`RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE\` default to the agent (SR-03). Too low a value locks out legitimate users behind one shared address (for example a class of students on one network, a High example in \`severity-scale.md\`); too high weakens SB-06.
- Options: 1. 60 per minute per client address and endpoint, fixed window, 429 with \`Retry-After\` (proposed default); 2. 10 per minute (stricter, risks locking out shared networks); 3. 300 per minute
- Human response: none
- Resolution: pending review (option 1 applied)

## D-11: Local compose stack runs with ORGANIZER_HTTPS_ONLY=false by default
- Timestamp: $T
- Phase: 2
- Type: non-blocking
- Trigger: SR-06 and \`environments.md\` allow HTTPS-only to be off only on local plain HTTP. With Docker Desktop port publishing the backend sees the Docker gateway address, not a loopback address, so with the setting on, the local export (E2E-05, DoD-P04) would always be refused. The backend's own default stays \`true\` and production refuses to start with \`false\`.

- Resolution: pending review (option 1 applied)

---
name: write-acceptance-tests
description: Write and freeze the black-box acceptance tests from the given acceptance criteria and end-to-end scenarios and the contracts, before any production code exists (phase 3).
---

> Owner: QA lead · Read in: phase 3 · Agent: read-only

- Reads: `project/01_requirements/acceptance-criteria.md`, `project/01_requirements/e2e-scenarios.md`, `docs/02_contracts/`, `general/quality/test-strategy.md`, `general/phases.md`
- Writes: acceptance and end-to-end tests, `docs/03_acceptance-manifest.sha256`, `docs/03_test-strategy.md`
- Does not read: production source code

## Procedure

1. For every AC, write at least one test through the component's public interface that checks the observable outcome the AC states. For a rejection AC, also check that nothing changed. For every scenario in `e2e-scenarios.md`, write exactly one end-to-end test; write no other end-to-end test, and do not split or merge scenarios.
2. Put the AC id in each test name.
3. Run the suite. Every test must fail because the behaviour is missing, not because of a build, configuration or harness error; a test that passes only on bootstrap code is listed in step 4. Fix the harness until that holds.
4. Record the run (pass/fail counts and a one-line reason per group of failures) in `docs/03_test-strategy.md`.
5. Self-check every assertion and helper before the freeze, because a defective frozen test costs a blocking decision: confirm that a correct implementation can make it pass, and that it cannot pass or fail for the wrong reason. Check what each helper returns and what each matcher compares (known cases: the PostgreSQL JDBC driver returns java.sql.Timestamp, not OffsetDateTime, for 	imestamptz unless the type is requested; AssertJ doesNotContain on a  yte[] tests single bytes, not a byte sequence, so compare the first bytes with Arrays.copyOf instead). A test must not contradict another assertion in the same test.
6. Format and lint the tests now; after freezing they cannot change.
7. Commit the tests story by story as you finish them. Then write the manifest (normalised line endings) and commit it alone as the freeze commit.

# Local stack (environments.md "local"): backend, frontend, PostgreSQL, Mailpit; plain HTTP on 127.0.0.1.
# Start from 02_output/: docker compose --env-file ../.env up -d --build
name: konferenca-registration

services:
  postgres:
    image: postgres:16.15-alpine
    environment:
      POSTGRES_DB: registration
      POSTGRES_USER: registration
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:?set POSTGRES_PASSWORD in .env}
    volumes:
      - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U registration -d registration"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 20

  mailpit:
    image: axllent/mailpit:v1.31.1
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:8025:8025"

  backend:
    build: ./backend
    environment:
      APP_ENVIRONMENT: local
      DB_URL: jdbc:postgresql://postgres:5432/registration
      DB_USER: registration
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:?set POSTGRES_PASSWORD in .env}
      SMTP_HOST: mailpit
      SMTP_PORT: "1025"
      SMTP_TLS: "false"
      MAIL_FROM: registration@konferenca.local
      ORGANIZER_EMAILS: ${ORGANIZER_EMAILS:?set ORGANIZER_EMAILS in .env}
      ORGANIZER_USERNAME: ${ORGANIZER_USERNAME:?set ORGANIZER_USERNAME in .env}
      ORGANIZER_PASSWORD: ${ORGANIZER_PASSWORD:?set ORGANIZER_PASSWORD in .env}
      JSON_COPY_DIR: /data/json-copies
      CAPTCHA_TEST_MODE: ${CAPTCHA_TEST_MODE:-true}
      RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY: ${RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY:-}
      RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY: ${RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY:-}
      RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE: ${RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE:-60}
      # Off only on local plain HTTP (SR-06, D-11); the backend default is true.
      ORGANIZER_HTTPS_ONLY: ${ORGANIZER_HTTPS_ONLY:-false}
    volumes:
      - jsoncopies:/data/json-copies
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:8080:8080"
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
      mailpit:
        condition: service_started

  frontend:
    build: ./frontend
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:8081:8080"
    depends_on:
      - backend

volumes:
  pgdata:
  jsoncopies:

# Test strategy (as executed)

> Written in: the test phases of the selected workflow, and phase 6 · Source: `general/quality/test-strategy.md`, workflow `rules.md` · Agent: writes

## Test levels as executed

| Level | Component | Location | Runner | Through | Frozen |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Acceptance | backend | `backend/src/test/java/si/konferenca/registration/acceptance/` (12 test classes, 102 tests) | JUnit 6 via `./mvnw test` | HTTP to the app on a random port (`@SpringBootTest`); PostgreSQL 16.15 and Mailpit 1.31.1 in Testcontainers; a JDK `HttpServer` as the mocked reCAPTCHA verify endpoint | yes |
| Acceptance | frontend | `frontend/src/acceptance/` (2 test files, 9 tests) | Vitest 4 + Testing Library, jsdom | the whole `<App />`; `fetch` replaced at the `/api` boundary | yes |
| End-to-end | all | `frontend/e2e/*.e2e.spec.ts` (5 tests, one per E2E-01 … E2E-05) | Playwright 1.63, Chromium | the browser and REST API against `docker compose` (`02_output/docker-compose.yml`); PostgreSQL via `psql` in the container, JSON copies via the backend container, mail via the Mailpit API, the workbook via a zip/XML reader | yes |
| Unit, integration, architecture | backend, frontend | any other test path | as above | internals | no (phase 5) |

AC coverage: every one of the 35 criteria is named by at least one acceptance test (backend for the API criteria, frontend for AC-001-08, AC-002-07, AC-004-01 … 04). DoD-P05 is covered by `CaptchaVerificationAcceptanceTest`.

### Harness assumptions (from the contracts; the implementation follows them)

| # | Assumption | Source |
|---|---|---|
| H-1 | The backend reads its settings by the names of spec section 4 (`DB_URL`, `SMTP_PORT`, `CONFERENCE_CONFIG_PATH`, …) as Spring placeholders, so tests pass them as properties. | spec §4 |
| H-2 | `CONFERENCE_CONFIG_PATH` accepts a plain absolute file path (and `classpath:` for the default). | spec §3.1 |
| H-3 | The JSON copy directory is not required at start; a write into it fails when the path is a regular file. | spec §3.2 step 5 |
| H-4 | The backend trusts `X-Forwarded-For` / `X-Forwarded-Proto` from loopback and private proxies (`server.forward-headers-strategy=native`). | spec §3.4 |
| H-5 | Option groups are `fieldset`/`legend` groups named "Workshops", "Events", "Meals", "Other activities"; option and consent checkboxes are labelled by their name or text. | interfaces "Registration form" 4, accessible names |
| H-6 | In test mode the captcha is a checkbox whose name contains "test mode" and yields the token `test-pass`. | interfaces "reCAPTCHA" |
| H-7 | A field error is linked to its input with `aria-describedby` and has `role="alert"`; an input without an error has no description. | interfaces "Registration form" |
| H-8 | Mailpit lists envelope-only recipients as `Bcc`; the injection test therefore checks the recipient set, not the absence of a `Bcc` header. | checked against Mailpit 1.31.1 in phase 3 |
| H-9 | The e2e run gets `ORGANIZER_USERNAME` / `ORGANIZER_PASSWORD` from the environment (exported from `.env` without printing). | working-rules "Secrets" |

### Self-check before the freeze

- Mailpit API field names, attachment download and delete-all were verified against a real `axllent/mailpit:v1.31.1` message (python `smtplib`).
- The e2e workbook reader was run on a workbook written by POI 5.5.1 (shared strings, empty cells, `&`, `<`, č š ž): rows came back exactly.
- Timestamps are read with `getObject(…, OffsetDateTime.class)`; JSON-copy vs database time is compared with 1 ms tolerance (PostgreSQL rounds to microseconds).
- The AC-003-03 cases first start the same settings with a valid file, so a refusal cannot come from another cause; on the skeleton they fail on that control start.
- Byte comparisons use `isEqualTo(byte[])` / `Buffer.equals` (whole content), never element-wise `doesNotContain`.

## Measurement exclusions

Fixed in phase 0 in the tool configuration (`backend/pom.xml` JaCoCo and PIT, `frontend/vite.config.ts` coverage), before any test was written; they equal the defaults of `quality-requirements.md` "Mutation scope".

| Path | Reason |
|---|---|
| `backend/src/main/java/si/konferenca/registration/RegistrationApplication.java` | `@SpringBootApplication` entry point, no logic |
| `frontend/src/main.tsx` | bootstrap file that only mounts the app |
| `frontend/src/**/*.d.ts` | type declarations |
| `frontend/src/**/*.test.{ts,tsx}`, `frontend/src/acceptance/**`, `frontend/src/test/**`, `frontend/e2e/**` | test code |

## First complete run (before any fix)

Phase 3 run on the bootstrap skeleton (commit before the freeze), logs in `out/logs/`.

| Suite | Passed | Failed | Reason (one line per group) |
|---|---|---|---|
| backend acceptance (`phase3-backend-first-run.log`) | 0 | 102 | the application context cannot start: the skeleton does not read the spec §4 settings (`DB_URL`), so no datasource ("Failed to determine a suitable driver class"); every behaviour is missing |
| frontend acceptance (vitest) | 0 | 9 | the skeleton page has no registration-type radio buttons (`findByRole("radio")` fails) |
| end-to-end (`phase3-e2e-first-run.log`) | 0 | 5 | E2E-01, 03, 04: no registration-type radio on the page; E2E-02: `/api/form-config` answers the proxy error page because the backend does not start; E2E-05: backend not listening on 8080 for the same reason |

No test passes on bootstrap code alone. Containers, compilation, type check, lint and formatting of all tests succeed, so no failure is a build or harness error.

## Final run (phase 6)

---
name: verify-release
description: Verify the finished system with evidence: definition of done, frozen tests, security baseline and scanners, secret leaks, runtime flows, traceability, and verify → fix → re-verify loops (phase 6).
---

> Owner: QA lead · Read in: phase 6 · Agent: read-only

- Reads: all of `01_input/`, `docs/`, source code
- Writes: `docs/06_verification-report.md` (findings `F-nn`)

## Procedure

1. Re-read the requirements (`project/01_requirements/*`, `docs/02_*`) before checking anything.
2. Recompute every hash in `docs/03_acceptance-manifest.sha256` and `docs/00_input-manifest.sha256`. Any mismatch is a Critical finding, whatever the reason.
3. Run the full test suite and every check command (ES-05). Coverage and mutation score were recorded in phase 5; re-measure them only for a component whose code or tests changed since, once, after the last fix, as `general/quality/measurement-scope.md` defines (including \
4. Start every component as described for its target environment and exercise the core user flows at runtime; record what was run and what was observed.
5. Security: for every `SB` and `SR` item, record where it is implemented and how it was checked (test, scan, or inspection). An item without evidence is a finding.
6. Run every scanner listed under `tooling` with a security purpose (dependency, static analysis, secrets); archive raw output in `out/logs/`. Run the dependency scan **online** with the NVD key from `.env` and never with Maven's `-o` (offline) flag: offline it reuses the report of phase 0 and the suppressions do not apply, which wastes a run.
7. Classify each finding with the severity scale. For a dependency vulnerability, check whether the vulnerable feature is used. If you propose lowering a Critical or High on that basis, record the evidence and raise a blocking decision.
8. Check logs and error responses produced during testing for personal data, secrets and internals. Then check that no `.env` value leaked, listing file names only and never the values (no output means clean; any name listed is a Critical finding):
   - files: `git ls-files -co --exclude-standard -z | xargs -0 grep -lF -f <(sed -n 's/^[A-Z_]*=//p' .env | tr -d '\r "'"'"'' | awk 'length>=6')`
   - commit messages: `git log --all --format=%B | grep -cF -f <(sed -n 's/^[A-Z_]*=//p' .env | tr -d '\r "'"'"'' | awk 'length>=6')` (must print `0`)
9. Run `node 01_input/00_general/skills/verify-release/trace-ac.mjs` once from the repository root: it prints the table AC → tests → commits (a test counts when its file names the AC or a range that contains it; a commit counts when its subject names the AC, a range that contains it, or its user story). Paste the output into the report and do not build the table by hand. An AC with no test or no commit is a finding. Commit size, message length and bursts are measured by the report afterwards, so do not audit commits here.
10. For each general and project DoD item, record evidence or a finding.
11. For every Critical or High finding, run verify → fix → re-verify and log each loop; triage Medium and Low as fixed, accepted with a reason, or open item.
12. Confirm every decision record has a resolution or is marked pending review.
13. State at the top of the report that it is a self-check, not an independent review.

docker compose exec -T backend sh -c "ls -l /data/json-copies/$EID.json /data/json-copies/$SID.json"
docker compose exec -T backend cat /data/json-copies/$SID.json; echo
echo "== DoD-P03 Mailpit (participant and organizer mails, organizer with JSON attachment)"
sleep 2; mails "$EID" "$SID"
echo "== DoD-P04 export"
curl -s -o "$S/export.xlsx" -w 'with credentials -> %{http_code} %{content_type}\n' -u "$U:$P" http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/export
python -c "
import zipfile,sys,re;z=zipfile.ZipFile(sys.argv[1]);print('valid workbook, parts:', ', '.join(n for n in z.namelist() if n.startswith('xl/')))
s=z.read('xl/sharedStrings.xml').decode(); rows=len(re.findall(r'<row ',z.read('xl/worksheets/sheet1.xml').decode()))
print('rows incl. header:', rows, '| contains Študent and Računalništvo:', 'Študent' in s and 'Računalništvo' in s)" "$S/export.xlsx"
echo "database rows: $(docker compose exec -T postgres psql -U registration -d registration -At -c 'SELECT count(*) FROM registration')"
echo "without credentials -> $(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}, %{size_download} bytes, %{content_type}' http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/export)"
echo "wrong password -> $(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -u "$U:wrong" http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/export)"
echo "== SB-10 headers: frontend /"; curl -s -I http://127.0.0.1:8081/ | grep -iE 'content-security|x-frame|x-content-type|referrer'
echo "== SB-10 headers: API"; curl -s -D - -o /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/form-config | grep -iE 'content-security|x-frame|x-content-type|referrer'
echo "== SR-08 a client Host header is not forwarded: Host evil.example via the frontend proxy -> $(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -H 'Host: evil.example' http://127.0.0.1:8081/api/form-config) (nginx sets Host backend:8080)"
echo "== SR-03 body limit: 20 KB -> $(python -c "print('{\"type\":\"'+'x'*20000+'\"}')" | curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @- http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/registrations)"
echo "== SB-11 non-root: backend uid $(docker compose exec -T backend id -u), frontend user $(docker compose exec -T frontend id -un)"
echo "== NFR-02 recreate every container"
docker compose down > /dev/null 2>&1; docker compose up -d > /dev/null 2>&1
for i in $(seq 1 60); do s=$(docker inspect -f '{{.State.Health.Status}}' konferenca-registration-backend-1 2>/dev/null); [ "$s" = healthy ] && break; sleep 3; done
docker compose ps --format '{{.Service}} {{.Status}}'
echo "after recreate, rows: $(docker compose exec -T postgres psql -U registration -d registration -At -c "SELECT count(*) FROM registration WHERE id IN ('$EID','$SID')") of 2; JSON copies: $(docker compose exec -T backend sh -c "ls /data/json-copies/$EID.json /data/json-copies/$SID.json | wc -l") of 2"
echo "== SR-03 rate limit (60 per minute per client and endpoint)"
codes=$(for i in $(seq 1 62); do curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} ' http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/form-config; done); echo "62 requests -> $(echo $codes | tr ' ' '\n' | sort | uniq -c | tr '\n' ' ')"
} > $L 2>&1; cat $L; for k in ORGANIZER_EMAILS ORGANIZER_PASSWORD ORGANIZER_USERNAME POSTGRES_PASSWORD NVD_API_KEY; do v="$(sed -n "s/^$k=//p" ../.env | tr -d '\r')"; grep -qF -- "$v" $L && echo "LEAK $k"; done; echo leak-check-done

# Conference registration

> Written in: phase 7 · Source: `project/02_design/architecture.md`, ES-06 · Agent: writes

## Overview

Online registration for a conference. External participants and students fill in their own form, choose workshops, events, meals and other activities from a configurable programme, and give the required consent. Every accepted registration is stored in PostgreSQL and as a raw JSON copy; the participant gets a confirmation email and every organizer a notification with the JSON attached. Organizers download all registrations as an Excel workbook. Registrations are protected by Google reCAPTCHA v2.

## Components

| Component | What it is | README |
|---|---|---|
| backend | Spring Boot 4.1 REST API under `/api` (Java 21): form configuration, registrations, export | [backend/README.md](backend/README.md) |
| frontend | React 19 single page built with Vite, served by nginx, which also forwards `/api/` to the backend | [frontend/README.md](frontend/README.md) |
| local stack | `docker-compose.yml`: backend, frontend, PostgreSQL 16, Mailpit (mail catcher) | this file |

## Quick start (local stack)

Prerequisites: Docker Engine with Docker Compose, and a `.env` file at the repository root copied from `01_input/01_project/00_setup/secrets.env.example` with `POSTGRES_PASSWORD`, `ORGANIZER_USERNAME`, `ORGANIZER_PASSWORD` (at least 16 characters) and `ORGANIZER_EMAILS` filled in.

```sh
cd 02_output
docker compose --env-file ../.env up -d --build
```

| URL | What |
|---|---|
| http://127.0.0.1:8081 | registration page |
| http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/form-config | API (backend directly) |
| http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/export | Excel export (HTTP Basic with `ORGANIZER_USERNAME` / `ORGANIZER_PASSWORD`) |
| http://127.0.0.1:8080/actuator/health/readiness | readiness |
| http://127.0.0.1:8025 | Mailpit: every email sent by the stack |

Locally the reCAPTCHA runs in test mode (a "test mode" checkbox on the page). The settings `CAPTCHA_TEST_MODE` (default `true` locally), `RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE` (default `60`) and `ORGANIZER_HTTPS_ONLY` (default `false` locally, D-11) can be overridden when starting, for example `RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE=1000 docker compose --env-file ../.env up -d`.

Stop with `docker compose --env-file ../.env down`; registrations and JSON copies stay on the named volumes `pgdata` and `jsoncopies` (`down -v` deletes them).

The end-to-end tests run against this stack: see [frontend/README.md](frontend/README.md#end-to-end-tests).

## Documentation

| Document | Content |
|---|---|
| [docs/02_specification.md](docs/02_specification.md) | architecture, behaviour, settings, deployment, traceability |
| [docs/02_contracts/](docs/02_contracts/) | OpenAPI, database schema, JSON copy and configuration schemas, emails, reCAPTCHA, UI |
| [docs/03_test-strategy.md](docs/03_test-strategy.md) | test levels, coverage and mutation results |
| [docs/06_verification-report.md](docs/06_verification-report.md) | definition of done, security evidence, findings |
| [docs/release-notes.md](docs/release-notes.md) | what is delivered, limitations, manual tests |
| [docs/decisions-log.md](docs/decisions-log.md) | every decision of the run |
| [docs/01_requirements-check.md](docs/01_requirements-check.md), [docs/00_preflight-report.md](docs/00_preflight-report.md) | requirements check, environment check |

- JDK 21 (pinned: Eclipse Temurin 21.0.10+7; this run built with Oracle JDK 21.0.11, D-02). Maven comes with the wrapper (`./mvnw`, Maven 3.9.9).
- Docker for the tests (Testcontainers starts PostgreSQL 16.15 and Mailpit 1.31.1).
- For `run`: a PostgreSQL database and an SMTP server, for example the local stack's (`docker compose --env-file ../.env up -d postgres mailpit` in `02_output/`; publish their ports or use the full stack instead).

## Configuration

All settings are environment variables (`docs/02_specification.md` section 4). Secrets come from `.env` (keys listed in `01_input/01_project/00_setup/secrets.env.example`) and have no default.

| Setting | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `APP_ENVIRONMENT` | `local` | `production` refuses unsafe settings at start (SR-02) |
| `DB_URL`, `DB_USER`, `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` | `jdbc:postgresql://localhost:5432/registration`, `registration`, none (secret) | |
| `SMTP_HOST`, `SMTP_PORT`, `SMTP_TLS`, `SMTP_USERNAME`, `SMTP_PASSWORD` | `localhost`, `1025`, `false`, empty, empty | SMTP account only in production (secret) |
| `MAIL_FROM` | `registration@konferenca.local` | |
| `ORGANIZER_EMAILS`, `ORGANIZER_USERNAME`, `ORGANIZER_PASSWORD` | none (secrets) | comma-separated recipients; export login |
| `CONFERENCE_CONFIG_PATH` | `classpath:conference.json` | options and consents, schema `docs/02_contracts/conference-config.schema.json`; an invalid file stops the start |
| `JSON_COPY_DIR` | `./data/json-copies` | persistent storage in production |
| `CAPTCHA_TEST_MODE` | `false` | `true` only locally and in tests: token `test-pass` |
| `RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY`, `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY` | empty (secrets) | required in production |
| `RECAPTCHA_VERIFY_URL` | Google siteverify | |
| `ORGANIZER_HTTPS_ONLY` | `true` | must stay `true` outside local plain HTTP (SR-06) |
| `ALLOWED_ORIGIN` | empty | CORS for the Vite dev server only |
| `RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE`, `REQUEST_MAX_BYTES` | `60`, `16384` | SR-03 |

## Commands (ES-05)

| Purpose | Command |
|---|---|
| build | `./mvnw -DskipTests package` (jar in `target/`) |
| test | `./mvnw verify` (unit, architecture and acceptance tests; JaCoCo report in `target/site/jacoco/`) |
| check | `./mvnw compile spotless:check pmd:check pmd:cpd-check spotbugs:check` (format with `./mvnw spotless:apply`) |
| run | `./mvnw spring-boot:run` with the settings above, for example `POSTGRES_PASSWORD=… ORGANIZER_USERNAME=… ORGANIZER_PASSWORD=… ORGANIZER_EMAILS=… CAPTCHA_TEST_MODE=true ./mvnw spring-boot:run` |
| mutation | `./mvnw org.pitest:pitest-maven:1.30.0:mutationCoverage -Dthreads=4` (about 25 minutes; report in `target/pit-reports/`) |
| dependency scan | `NVD_API_KEY=… ./mvnw org.owasp:dependency-check-maven:12.1.0:check` (online; suppressions in `dependency-check-suppressions.xml`) |
| container | `docker build -t registration-backend .` (multi-stage, runs as uid 10001) |

## Troubleshooting

- `Could not resolve placeholder 'POSTGRES_PASSWORD'` (or an organizer setting): the secret is not set in the environment.
- `Invalid conference configuration: …` at start: the options file does not match its schema; the message names the entry.
- `Refusing to start in production: …`: a setting listed in the message is unsafe for `APP_ENVIRONMENT=production`.
- Tests fail with Docker errors: start Docker; Testcontainers needs it.
- `GET /api/export` answers 403 with valid credentials: `ORGANIZER_HTTPS_ONLY=true` and the request is plain HTTP from a non-local address; use HTTPS through the proxy.
- 429 responses: more than `RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE` requests per minute from one client to one endpoint.

# Frontend

> Written in: phase 7 · Source: `project/02_design/architecture.md`, ES-05, ES-06 · Agent: writes

React 19 single page for the registration form (`docs/02_contracts/interfaces.md`, "Registration form"), built with Vite and served by nginx. It talks to the backend only through `/api` (AR-01) and holds no secret: the reCAPTCHA site key comes from `GET /api/form-config` (AR-07).

## Prerequisites

- Node.js 24.13.0 with npm 11.6.2 (`engine-strict` is on).
- For `run`: the backend on `http://127.0.0.1:8080` (the Vite dev server proxies `/api` there).
- For the end-to-end tests: the local stack (root [README](../README.md)) and Playwright's Chromium (`npx playwright install chromium` once, if it is missing).

## Configuration

The frontend has no settings of its own. nginx (`nginx.conf`) forwards `/api/` to `backend:8080` with a fixed `Host` (SR-08), limits bodies to 16 KiB and adds the security headers. In production the external reverse proxy serves `/` from this container and forwards `/api` to the backend.

## Commands (ES-05)

| Purpose | Command |
|---|---|
| install | `npm ci` |
| build | `npm run build` (type check, then `dist/`) |
| test | `npm test` (unit and acceptance tests, Vitest); `npm run coverage` for the v8 report in `coverage/` |
| check | `npm run check` (Prettier, ESLint, `tsc --noEmit`); format with `npm run format` |
| run | `npm run dev` (http://127.0.0.1:5173) |
| mutation | `npm run mutation` (Stryker, about 17 minutes; report in `reports/mutation/`) |
| duplication | `npm run duplication` |
| dependency scan | `npm audit` |
| container | `docker build -t registration-frontend .` (nginx as user `nginx`, port 8080) |

## End-to-end tests

The five tests in `e2e/` (E2E-01 … E2E-05) need the running local stack. They read the database and the JSON copies through `docker compose exec`, so Compose must find `.env`, and the export check needs the organizer login. Set both from `.env` without printing them, from `02_output/frontend` in Git Bash:

```sh
export COMPOSE_ENV_FILES="$(cd ../.. && pwd)/.env"
export ORGANIZER_USERNAME="$(sed -n 's/^ORGANIZER_USERNAME=//p' ../../.env | tr -d '\r')"
export ORGANIZER_PASSWORD="$(sed -n 's/^ORGANIZER_PASSWORD=//p' ../../.env | tr -d '\r')"
npm run e2e
```

## Troubleshooting

- "The registration form could not be loaded": the backend is not reachable through `/api` (check `docker compose ps`, or start the backend for `npm run dev`).
- `npm ci` fails with an engine error: use Node 24.13.0 / npm 11.6.2.
- e2e: `required variable … is missing a value`: `COMPOSE_ENV_FILES` is not set; `Set ORGANIZER_USERNAME and ORGANIZER_PASSWORD`: export them as shown above.
- e2e: many 429 answers: the stack's rate limit (60 per minute) was hit by repeated runs; wait a minute or start the stack with a higher `RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE`.

# Conference registration

> Written in: phase 7 · Source: `project/02_design/architecture.md`, ES-06 · Agent: writes

## Overview

Online registration for a conference. External participants and students fill in their own form, choose workshops, events, meals and other activities from a configurable programme, and give the required consent. Every accepted registration is stored in PostgreSQL and as a raw JSON copy; the participant gets a confirmation email and every organizer a notification with the JSON attached. Organizers download all registrations as an Excel workbook. Registrations are protected by Google reCAPTCHA v2.

## Components

| Component | What it is | README |
|---|---|---|
| backend | Spring Boot 4.1 REST API under `/api` (Java 21): form configuration, registrations, export | [backend/README.md](backend/README.md) |
| frontend | React 19 single page built with Vite, served by nginx, which also forwards `/api/` to the backend | [frontend/README.md](frontend/README.md) |
| local stack | `docker-compose.yml`: backend, frontend, PostgreSQL 16, Mailpit (mail catcher) | this file |

## Quick start (local stack)

Prerequisites: Docker Engine with Docker Compose, and a `.env` file at the repository root copied from `01_input/01_project/00_setup/secrets.env.example` with `POSTGRES_PASSWORD`, `ORGANIZER_USERNAME`, `ORGANIZER_PASSWORD` (at least 16 characters) and `ORGANIZER_EMAILS` filled in.

```sh
cd 02_output
docker compose --env-file ../.env up -d --build
```

| URL | What |
|---|---|
| http://127.0.0.1:8081 | registration page |
| http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/form-config | API (backend directly) |
| http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/export | Excel export (HTTP Basic with `ORGANIZER_USERNAME` / `ORGANIZER_PASSWORD`) |
| http://127.0.0.1:8080/actuator/health/readiness | readiness |
| http://127.0.0.1:8025 | Mailpit: every email sent by the stack |

Locally the reCAPTCHA runs in test mode (a "test mode" checkbox on the page). The settings `CAPTCHA_TEST_MODE` (default `true` locally), `RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE` (default `60`) and `ORGANIZER_HTTPS_ONLY` (default `false` locally, D-11) can be overridden when starting, for example `RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE=1000 docker compose --env-file ../.env up -d`.

Stop with `docker compose --env-file ../.env down`; registrations and JSON copies stay on the named volumes `pgdata` and `jsoncopies` (`down -v` deletes them).

The end-to-end tests run against this stack: see [frontend/README.md](frontend/README.md#end-to-end-tests).

## Documentation

| Document | Content |
|---|---|
| [docs/02_specification.md](docs/02_specification.md) | architecture, behaviour, settings, deployment, traceability |
| [docs/02_contracts/](docs/02_contracts/) | OpenAPI, database schema, JSON copy and configuration schemas, emails, reCAPTCHA, UI |
| [docs/03_test-strategy.md](docs/03_test-strategy.md) | test levels, coverage and mutation results |
| [docs/06_verification-report.md](docs/06_verification-report.md) | definition of done, security evidence, findings |
| [docs/release-notes.md](docs/release-notes.md) | what is delivered, limitations, manual tests |
| [docs/decisions-log.md](docs/decisions-log.md) | every decision of the run |
| [docs/01_requirements-check.md](docs/01_requirements-check.md), [docs/00_preflight-report.md](docs/00_preflight-report.md) | requirements check, environment check |

- Node.js 24.13.0 with npm 11.6.2 (`engine-strict` is on).
- For `run`: the backend on `http://127.0.0.1:8080` (the Vite dev server proxies `/api` there).
- For the end-to-end tests: the local stack (root [README](../README.md)) and Playwright's Chromium (`npx playwright install chromium` once, if it is missing).

## Configuration

The frontend has no settings of its own. nginx (`nginx.conf`) forwards `/api/` to `backend:8080` with a fixed `Host` (SR-08), limits bodies to 16 KiB and adds the security headers. In production the external reverse proxy serves `/` from this container and forwards `/api` to the backend.

## Commands (ES-05)

| Purpose | Command |
|---|---|
| install | `npm ci` |
| build | `npm run build` (type check, then `dist/`) |
| test | `npm test` (unit and acceptance tests, Vitest); `npm run coverage` for the v8 report in `coverage/` |
| check | `npm run check` (Prettier, ESLint, `tsc --noEmit`); format with `npm run format` |
| run | `npm run dev` (http://127.0.0.1:5173) |
| mutation | `npm run mutation` (Stryker, about 17 minutes; report in `reports/mutation/`) |
| duplication | `npm run duplication` |
| dependency scan | `npm audit` |
| container | `docker build -t registration-frontend .` (nginx as user `nginx`, port 8080) |

## End-to-end tests

The five tests in `e2e/` (E2E-01 … E2E-05) need the running local stack. They read the database and the JSON copies through `docker compose exec`, so Compose must find `.env`, and the export check needs the organizer login. Set both from `.env` without printing them, from `02_output/frontend` in Git Bash:

```sh
export COMPOSE_ENV_FILES="$(cd ../.. && pwd)/.env"
export ORGANIZER_USERNAME="$(sed -n 's/^ORGANIZER_USERNAME=//p' ../../.env | tr -d '\r')"
export ORGANIZER_PASSWORD="$(sed -n 's/^ORGANIZER_PASSWORD=//p' ../../.env | tr -d '\r')"
npm run e2e
```

## Troubleshooting

- "The registration form could not be loaded": the backend is not reachable through `/api` (check `docker compose ps`, or start the backend for `npm run dev`).
- `npm ci` fails with an engine error: use Node 24.13.0 / npm 11.6.2.
- e2e: `required variable … is missing a value`: `COMPOSE_ENV_FILES` is not set; `Set ORGANIZER_USERNAME and ORGANIZER_PASSWORD`: export them as shown above.
- e2e: many 429 answers: the stack's rate limit (60 per minute) was hit by repeated runs; wait a minute or start the stack with a higher `RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE`.

input.content:
# Release notes

> Written in: phase 7 · Agent: writes

Version 1.0.0 of the conference registration (backend and frontend), 2026-10-21.

## Delivered

- Registration forms for external participants (US-001) and students (US-002) with exactly the fixed fields of each type, the options available to the type grouped as workshops, events, meals and other activities, and the mandatory `privacy` consent, never preselected.
- Conference options and consents from a configuration file (`CONFERENCE_CONFIG_PATH`, schema in `docs/02_contracts/conference-config.schema.json`); an invalid file stops the backend at start (US-003).
- Confirmation in the page only after the backend accepted the registration; field errors next to their fields; a general message without technical details on failures (US-004).
- Storage in PostgreSQL and as a raw JSON copy per registration, both before the success answer (US-005, AR-05).
- Participant confirmation email and one organizer notification per configured address with the JSON copy attached; a mail failure never undoes a registration (US-006, US-007).
- Excel export for the organizer over HTTP Basic, refused over plain HTTP from non-local clients (US-008, SR-06).
- reCAPTCHA v2 verified on the backend, a deterministic test mode for local and test use, rate and body-size limits, security headers, non-root containers, health and readiness endpoints.
- Local stack with `docker compose` (backend, frontend, PostgreSQL, Mailpit); data on named volumes survives container recreation.

Verification: 35/35 acceptance criteria tested; 311 automated tests green (backend 251, frontend 55, end-to-end 5); line coverage backend 99.11 %, frontend 100 %; mutation score backend 99.10 % adjusted (96.70 % raw), frontend 90.85 %; no open Critical or High finding (`docs/06_verification-report.md`).

## Known limitations

- Medium, accepted (`docs/06_verification-report.md`): the pinned Vite 6.4.3 has advisory GHSA-698v-4r3x-3vcv in its dev server (not in the shipped bundle; fix 6.4.4 needs approval, D-16); `qs` advisories only through Stryker (PA-03); nginx `/api/` location without `internal`; no npm `min-release-age` (needs npm 11.10).
- The rate limit is kept in memory per backend instance and counts per client address and endpoint; behind several backend instances the limit applies per instance.
- Email addresses are accepted with an ASCII domain only (D-09); text fields are limited to 200 characters, email to 254 (D-08).
- The local stack runs with `ORGANIZER_HTTPS_ONLY=false` (D-11); production refuses that setting.
- Registrations and JSON copies are never deleted automatically (OQ-06): **the operator must delete the database rows and the JSON copies no later than 12 months after the conference.**
- The end-to-end tests are not part of the mutation runs (D-15).
- Built and tested on the host with Oracle JDK 21.0.11 and Docker Compose 5.6.0 instead of the pinned Temurin 21.0.10+7 and Compose 5.5.1 (approved, D-02, D-03); the images use the pinned Temurin.

## Must be tested manually by a human

From `project/00_setup/environments.md`, "External services":

1. **Google reCAPTCHA v2 with production keys:** set `CAPTCHA_TEST_MODE=false`, `RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY` and `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY`; the page shows the Google widget; one real registration succeeds; a registration without solving the widget is refused.
2. **SMTP delivery to a real mailbox:** with the production SMTP settings (`SMTP_HOST`, `SMTP_PORT`, `SMTP_TLS=true`, `SMTP_USERNAME`, `SMTP_PASSWORD`), the participant confirmation and the organizer notification with the JSON attachment arrive in real mailboxes and are not marked as spam.
3. **TLS and the reverse proxy:** the external nginx with Let's Encrypt serves `/` from the frontend over HTTPS, redirects HTTP to HTTPS, forwards `/api` to the backend, sets the upstream `Host` itself (SR-08) and sends `X-Forwarded-Proto: https`; the organizer export works over HTTPS and is refused (403) over plain HTTP.

# Conference registration

> Written in: phase 7 · Source: `project/02_design/architecture.md`, ES-06 · Agent: writes

## Overview

Online registration for a conference. External participants and students fill in their own form, choose workshops, events, meals and other activities from a configurable programme, and give the required consent. Every accepted registration is stored in PostgreSQL and as a raw JSON copy; the participant gets a confirmation email and every organizer a notification with the JSON attached. Organizers download all registrations as an Excel workbook. Registrations are protected by Google reCAPTCHA v2.

## Components

| Component | What it is | README |
|---|---|---|
| backend | Spring Boot 4.1 REST API under `/api` (Java 21): form configuration, registrations, export | [backend/README.md](backend/README.md) |
| frontend | React 19 single page built with Vite, served by nginx, which also forwards `/api/` to the backend | [frontend/README.md](frontend/README.md) |
| local stack | `docker-compose.yml`: backend, frontend, PostgreSQL 16, Mailpit (mail catcher) | this file |

## Quick start (local stack)

Prerequisites: Docker Engine with Docker Compose, and a `.env` file at the repository root copied from `01_input/01_project/00_setup/secrets.env.example` with `POSTGRES_PASSWORD`, `ORGANIZER_USERNAME`, `ORGANIZER_PASSWORD` (at least 16 characters) and `ORGANIZER_EMAILS` filled in.

```sh
cd 02_output
docker compose --env-file ../.env up -d --build
```

| URL | What |
|---|---|
| http://127.0.0.1:8081 | registration page |
| http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/form-config | API (backend directly) |
| http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/export | Excel export (HTTP Basic with `ORGANIZER_USERNAME` / `ORGANIZER_PASSWORD`) |
| http://127.0.0.1:8080/actuator/health/readiness | readiness |
| http://127.0.0.1:8025 | Mailpit: every email sent by the stack |

Locally the reCAPTCHA runs in test mode (a "test mode" checkbox on the page). The settings `CAPTCHA_TEST_MODE` (default `true` locally), `RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE` (default `60`) and `ORGANIZER_HTTPS_ONLY` (default `false` locally, D-11) can be overridden when starting, for example `RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE=1000 docker compose --env-file ../.env up -d`.

Stop with `docker compose --env-file ../.env down`; registrations and JSON copies stay on the named volumes `pgdata` and `jsoncopies` (`down -v` deletes them).

The end-to-end tests run against this stack: see [frontend/README.md](frontend/README.md#end-to-end-tests).

## Documentation

| Document | Content |
|---|---|
| [docs/02_specification.md](docs/02_specification.md) | architecture, behaviour, settings, deployment, traceability |
| [docs/02_contracts/](docs/02_contracts/) | OpenAPI, database schema, JSON copy and configuration schemas, emails, reCAPTCHA, UI |
| [docs/03_test-strategy.md](docs/03_test-strategy.md) | test levels, coverage and mutation results |
| [docs/06_verification-report.md](docs/06_verification-report.md) | definition of done, security evidence, findings |
| [docs/release-notes.md](docs/release-notes.md) | what is delivered, limitations, manual tests |
| [docs/decisions-log.md](docs/decisions-log.md) | every decision of the run |
| [docs/01_requirements-check.md](docs/01_requirements-check.md), [docs/00_preflight-report.md](docs/00_preflight-report.md) | requirements check, environment check |
